articles.summary: Clavicular, the "looksmaxxing" influencer and streamer whose real name is Braden Peters, has been charged with one count each of rape, drugging a person for sexual intercourse and providing alcohol…

image.caption: Clavicular walks the runway during the 424 Menswear Spring/Summer 2027 show as part of Paris Fashion Week on June 23, 2026. (Francois Durand/Getty Images)

blocks.text: Entertainment·New

Clavicular, the "looksmaxxing" influencer and streamer whose real name is Braden Peters, has been charged with one count each of rape, drugging a person for sexual intercourse and providing alcohol to a minor, according to online court records viewed by CBC News.
Reps for the influencer say he has not been physically served
The charges against the 20-year-old were filed on Sept. 8 in a Cape Cod, Mass., courthouse. The alleged incidents occurred on May 23, 2025, according to the records.
An arraignment is set for Oct. 14 and Peters is not currently in custody. The alleged victim is not named in the filings, in accordance with Massachusetts law.
Has looksmaxxing guru Clavicular gone too far?

The charges were first reported by the U.S. outlet The Bulwark. Responding to the Bulwark report, Peters’s representative wrote in a statement to The Hollywood Reporter that "Clavicular has not been physically served. As usual, The Bulwark is exaggerating the status of a case to boost traffic. We appreciate the Hollywood Reporter for fact-checking."

In a statement to CBC News, Peters's representative also suggested the charges are in relation to a previous civil complaint filed in Miami by a woman named Aleksandra Vasilevna Mendoza. Mendoza accused Peters of battery, fraud and sexual misconduct in relation to events that took place in 2025.

According to legal filings obtained by CBC News, Mendoza previously alleged that the streamer injected her face with Aqualyx without consent when she was a minor. Aqualyx is a fat-dissolving substance not approved by the FDA. She also alleged Peters had sex with her when she was "knowingly intoxicated" and without her consent.
"THE TIMELINE: She files a lawsuit and doesn’t include sexual assault as a count. Then she amends it and adds it a couple of months later," representatives for Peters wrote in an email to CBC News.

"Clavicular then filed a motion to dismiss fighting the civil lawsuit because letter/text messages show she knew what was happening with the injections and he refused to pay money. She and her lawyer then go to police."
Clavicular calls legal filings 'petty'
Peters has become well-known on the internet for his "looksmaxxing" content. He's part of a community that promotes tips for people to improve their attractiveness.
In Clavicular's case, this includes taking steroids and peptide injections and even breaking facial bones in pursuit of more defined features. He has more than a million followers on TikTok.

items: How looksmaxxing can harm young men and boys
Your teen is likely seeing 'looksmaxxing' content online. Here's what you need to know
The Rise of ‘Looksmaxxing’

blocks.text: His content has gained attention for how extreme and dangerous it can be.
Peters took to social media on Monday following the news of the criminal charges.
"Trying to get my attention in anyway possible, a lawsuit? Seriously… really petty of you," he wrote on X.

Alongside the post, he added a video of Mendoza calling him "super nice," and a letter she allegedly wrote to him saying she is "super thankful" for him "helping me as much as you have been." The streamer also posted a clip from a livestream where Mendoza says she was 18, though the date it was filmed is not clear.
"Happens to all successful young men, people try to come for your money," Clavicular wrote in another X post. "Greed is evil."

This is not the first time the influencer has been criminally charged. In April, Peters was charged with unlawfully discharging a firearm, stemming from a video of him shooting an alligator in the Florida Everglades.
He was also hospitalized earlier this year after appearing to overdose during a livestream.
ABOUT THE AUTHOR
Griffin Jaeger is a reporter and producer with CBC's entertainment unit. He also formerly hosted and produced content for The National’s digital platforms. You can reach him at griffin.jaeger@cbc.ca

articles.title: EU removes oligarchs from Russia sanctions list as deadline looms
articles.summary:
Alisher Usmanov and Mikhail Fridman delisted in what Ireland’s EU presidency called ‘a difficult compromise’ for the bloc

The EU has agreed to remove two Russian billionaires, Alisher…

blocks.text: The EU has agreed to remove two Russian billionaires, Alisher Usmanov and Mikhail Fridman, from its sanctions list, while extending restrictions on nearly 3,000 individuals and companies accused of supporting the war on Ukraine for the next three years.

With an end-of-Tuesday deadline looming to preserve the Russia blacklist, the EU’s 27 member states found a compromise that meant delisting the two oligarchs in spite of very few countries wanting this outcome. EU sanctions have to be approved unanimously.

France stunned and infuriated EU governments this month when it called for Usmanov, a Russian-Uzbek national, to be removed from the list on “national security” grounds, reported to refer to a prisoner exchange deal involving French nationals and Azerbaijan.
Luxembourg then asked for the same treatment for Fridman, the Russian-Israeli magnate, who is suing the Grand Duchy for $16bn (£12bn) for freezing his assets.
The exemptions angered many EU countries that believe it sets a bad precedent by allowing member states to weaken sanctions in defence of national interests.

Ukraine criticised the removal of the men from the sanctions list as unacceptable. Shortly after the decision emerged, Ukraine’s president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, wrote on social media: “No name on the sanctions list is there by accident: each one represents a reason why this war started and continues to this day”.

The Ukrainian foreign minister, Andrii Sybiha, called the decision “shameful and unjustifiable” on X. “Moscow is celebrating because it got what it wanted: a sense ‌of impunity, the humiliation of the EU, and division among Europeans,” he added.
In order to enable the delistings that many EU member states found unpalatable, it was proposed that the sanctions be rolled over for 36 months, rather than the usual six.

A spokesperson for Ireland’s EU presidency, which brokered the talks, said the bloc had reached “a difficult compromise”. They said: “Until now, these listings have been reviewed and assessed on a six-monthly basis; today’s decision to renew on a 36-month basis enhances the durability and predictability of the EU sanctions framework.”

A decision had been expected earlier this week, but Latvia’s government, facing parliamentary elections on 3 October, announced a last-minute objection to the delistings on Monday. Latvia’s prime minister, Andris Kulbergs, said late on Monday night that he could not accept the proposed compromise and instructed his foreign minister to enter talks with Paris and Brussels to find a solution.

Diplomats said Latvia had finally agreed to abstain on the two delistings. The blacklist includes Russia’s president, Vladimir Putin, and foreign minister, Sergey Lavrov, as well as Duma deputies, the country’s major banks, energy companies and military industrial complex.

Senior EU officials have promised to present about 1,600 new designations – individuals and entities involved in the Russian military industrial complex – to foreign ministers next month. But the latest standoff, which followed the tortuous agreement on the EU’s 21st round of sanctions in July, suggests the process could be difficult.

articles.title: 'What he’s doing is positively un-American': Late-night hosts react to Trump media ban
articles.summary: The comedians of late-night television have a vested interest in protecting the First Amendment. So when U.S. President Donald Trump announced he was banning news outlets CNN, MS NOW, and Politico…

image.caption: Late-night television comedians NBC's Seth Meyers, ABC's Jimmy Kimmel, NBC's Jimmy Fallon, and Comedy Central's Jon Stewart accused U.S. President Donald Trump of tramping on the constitutionally protected freedom of the press with his White House media ban. (NBC/ABC/NBC/Comedy Central/ YouTube)

blocks.text: Entertainment·New

The comedians of late-night television have a vested interest in protecting the First Amendment. So when U.S. President Donald Trump announced he was banning news outlets CNN, MS NOW, and Politico from the White House last Friday, they came out swinging.
Comedians try to find humour in Trump's decision to bar CNN, Politico, MS NOW from White House
Jon Stewart, Seth Meyers, Jimmy Kimmel and even — to some extent — the famously "not very political" Jimmy Fallon have built their careers making fun of the U.S. president.

So when Donald Trump announced he was banning news outlets CNN, MS NOW, and Politico from the White House last Friday, the late-night television hosts came out swinging in defence of the First Amendment, which protects freedom of speech and the press.
Were they outraged? Definitely. Were they funny? You be judge.
"The White House press pool is more of a mess than the reflecting pool right now," said Jimmy Kimmel, whose jokes have landed him in trouble with the Trump administration before.
"What he's doing is positively un-American," he said on ABC's Jimmy Kimmel Live!

"The five networks, including Fox, joined forces to put out a statement saying the public has a vital interest in receiving accurate, independent information about its government.... Do you realize how far south somebody has to go for Fox News to defend CNN?" he added.
Helipad event offers fodder for jokes

Both Kimmel and NBC host Seth Meyers pointed out how Trump's media ban appeared to backfire when the White House press pool, which usually has eyes on the president at all official events, refused to cover his opening of a new helicopter landing pad.

There were visuals of the ribbon cutting from the White House's own video stream, but there was no microphone there to pick up what the president was saying. All that could be heard was the whirring of the helicopter blades.
"The best is, that sound is always the substance of what Trump is saying," said Meyers.

Yesterday, the Trump administration released a statement reiterating its position that, "White House access is a privilege — not a right" and rejecting claims the media ban undermined reporters' First Amendment rights.
That argument was put to Trump directly by some of the journalists remaining in the White House.
Acting like a diva
Meyers played a clip of Trump's response, saying the president "sounds like an aging Hollywood starlet chewing out a director for cutting her line."
Jimmy Fallon compared him to the host of The Traitors. "He even dressed like Alan Cumming to tell them, 'You're banished from my castle.'"

He also suggested the First Lady wished she, too, would be banished to get away from her husband. "In a related story, Melania just applied to be a reporter for CNN, MSN NOW and Politico," joked Fallon.
On The Daily Show, Jon Stewart focused on Trump's reason for the media ban: his disappointment in the outlets' negative news stories.
Outrage and incredulity

"Have you tried president-ing better?" asked Stewart. "I mean give the press something to work with. Oh, here's a positive story: I never thought my car could take $140 worth of gas in such a small tank!"
Stewart toggled between outrage and incredulity as he replayed footage of Trump justifying his media ban.
"Not for nothing, have we ever had a president just flat out in the Oval Office come out against the Constitution?"
ABOUT THE AUTHOR

Helen Surgenor is a producer for CBC News based in Toronto, currently working for the entertainment unit. She spent years waking up before dawn to make the daily news podcast World Report. She has reported in Alberta, Iqaluit and Barbados. You can reach her at helen.surgenor@cbc.ca.

articles.title: Cyclist who dressed as man to avoid Taliban wins silver medal
articles.summary: Afghan cyclist Fariba Hashimi wins silver in the women's road race at the Asian Games, having fled oppression in her home country to pursue a sporting dream.

blocks.text: Hashimi followed her sister Yulduz, also an international cyclist, into the sport at the age of 15, despite danger in their home province of Faryab.
"I always dressed as a man to go to training, wearing two or three different masks so ‌people ⁠would not recognise or attack me," Hashimi previously told Reuters., external
Hashimi said she would have to avoid stones being thrown at her whilst riding her bike.
Hashimi now lives and trains in Italy thanks to help from the Italian former world champion Alessandra Cappellotto.
Looking back at life in Afghanistan, Hashimi said the Taliban "took away our freedom".
"This silver medal can show a lot of resilience from Afghan women, and I'm really happy," she said.
"I'm not alone, I know that behind me millions of women, from many countries, have the same dream and they are standing with me."
Hashimi and her sister competed at the 2024 Paris Olympics and are now setting their sights on the 2028 Los Angeles Games.
"I never want to give up," Hashimi said, "and hopefully we can see [what can happen] again in Los Angeles."

articles.title: Military commander vows fast action on AI and robots, sees 'untapped potential' for Canada
articles.summary: A top Canadian forces commander says the military is ramping up purchases of low-cost, autonomous and reusable weapons systems. The push comes as world leaders and major tech executives debate if AI…

image.caption: Lt.-Gen. Darcy Molstad, commander of Canadian Joint Forces Command, speaks at the Ottawa Conference on Security and Defence on March 5, 2026. (Spencer Colby/The Canadian Press)

blocks.text: Business·New

A top Canadian forces commander says the military is ramping up purchases of low-cost, autonomous and reusable weapons systems. The push comes as world leaders and major tech executives debate if AI technology is advancing too quickly.
At robotics conference, commander of Canadian Joint Forces Command says 'imagination is your only limitation'
A top Canadian Forces commander says the military will rapidly buy more low-cost, autonomous and reusable weapons systems and equipment as it faces a rising tide of global threats.

Lt.-Gen. Darcy Molstad, commander of Canadian Joint Forces Command (CJFC), spoke at the Canadian Robotics Council 2026 Symposium on Monday, telling members of Canada's tech industry to stand by for a surge in purchase orders amid a "massive recapitalization of major platforms."

"This industry in Canada has so much untapped potential," the former fighter pilot told a room full of robotics entrepreneurs attending a panel discussion in Toronto. "Your imagination is your only limitation on the use cases for robotics paired with AI."
Molstad's remarks about embracing artificial intelligence-powered military hardware come as world leaders and prominent tech executives debate how to handle rapid advances in AI safely.

Powerful AI models have escaped human control, as was the case in July, when OpenAI agents hacked into a rival firm. Some leaders, including OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, say the technology is evolving too fast.
Supply depots stuck in the 1980s

While autonomous hardware like drones are frequently associated with front-line combat, Molstad spelled out potential across the military, including medical diagnostic support, supply depot logistics and automated military police vehicle inspections.

"We see MPs [military police] that are inspecting vehicles with a mirror underneath the car. I'm pretty sure that's a use case for a robot with AI integrated to do that — and a lot better than humans can do it," he said.

"Our supply depots are still locked, in some ways, in the '80s and '90s technologies. We do not necessarily need to recreate an Amazon fulfilment centre, but we need to move from the '80s to something in between that is suitable for defence needs."

items: Is AI evolving too fast? A look at the debate on slowing it down
Canada is investing $150M to make AI safer. Will it work?

blocks.text: On the combat side, Molstad said CJFC has already established a list of 399 pre-qualified vendors for the Canadian military's Defence Drone Initiative. He expects more formal requests for proposals (RFPs) will follow as Canada's military leans deeper into new technologies.
"We're closer to a major global conflict than we've ever been in [the] history of our country since the major wars," he said.

"We have to modernize as fast as we possibly can to give our soldiers, sailors, aviators and special operators the tools that they need to be able to deter. Because none of us want to actually fight a war."

Molstad was joined Monday by Duncan Stewart, a special executive advisor on innovation and industry to the Canadian Armed Forces. Stewart is also a partner at the Business Development Bank of Canada's $200-million tech venture fund, which backs early-stage startups.

"[The] government is a very fickle customer. It's a very tricky customer to deal with from an industry perspective," said Stewart. "Government tends to move very slowly. It tends to be very risk averse, and it tends to buy things in fits and starts."

Stewart added that Canada's traditional military suppliers tend to be large companies, which often lack the agility of the smaller firms he represents. "A lot of the innovation that we're seeing come from the cutting edge, especially in autonomous systems, is coming from small [companies]," he said

items: The drone war comes home: Canada scrambles to shield military bases in legal grey zone
Zelenskyy's comparison of Canada to Ukraine is imperfect — but it matters

blocks.text: Molstad cited the military's Defense Drone Initiative as evidence the government is "doing things differently" now.

"We need to figure out how to get the right industries with security clearances to understand what our concepts of operations are … the threats that we are facing at a classified level, so that you can actually do the work that you need to do to come up with the innovative, novel solutions that we're not thinking about," he said.
In February, Ottawa released its new defence industrial strategy. The plan includes a goal to award 70 per cent of federal defence contracts to Canadian firms within a decade.

Prime Minister Mark Carney has said the policy will better equip the military, while countering U.S. President Donald Trump's effort to make the United States the arms-maker of choice to allied countries.
'Stand by for G-forces'
Molstad borrowed language from his time flying CF-18s as he told robotics and AI entrepreneurs about the Canadian military's plan to pick up the pace.
"The ex-fighter pilot in me will say, 'stand by for G, stand by for G-forces,'" he said.

"Because when we issue an RFP — the ones that we issued just recently — we're giving five days for you to respond. We're giving you the statutory minimum to respond, because this is how fast we need to move."
Quebec will be home to a new facility for military drone research
Looking ahead, Molstad said the industry can expect "a steady drumbeat of RFPs for robotic and autonomous systems over the course of the next five years."
Earlier this month, Canada and Ukraine signed an expansive 100-year partnership that lays the foundation for the construction of millions of drones by manufacturers in the two countries.

Carney has said Ukraine's war with Russia marks a turning point in modern warfare, with unmanned weapons systems proving their worth in the hands of Ukrainian soldiers by reaching targets hundreds of kilometres inside of Russia.

Back in Canada, at an isolated location west of Ottawa, Molstad oversaw an exercise last month where dozens of drone manufacturers were put through their paces by members of the Canadian Armed Forces.
"Robotic and autonomous systems are the way of the future," Molstad said Monday. "We have to do it responsibly, with the right policies and checks in play."
ABOUT THE AUTHOR

Jeff Lagerquist is a senior writer with CBC News based in Toronto. Originally from Erin, Ont., he studied journalism at Toronto Metropolitan University. Jeff previously worked as a senior reporter for Yahoo Finance Canada. He was also a reporter and digital producer for CTV National News, BNN Bloomberg and The Financial Post. He was also a Columbia University energy journalism fellow for 2025.

articles.title: Top South African policeman charged with sexual offences
articles.summary: Shadrack Sibiya, who has made no comment, is alleged to have groomed a 16-year-old and raped an 18-year-old.

blocks.text: One of South Africa's highest ranking police officers has been charged with sexual offences at a brief appearance at a court north-west of Johannesburg.

The charges relate to allegations that Lt Gen Shadrack Sibiya sexually groomed a 16-year-old girl and raped an 18-year-old woman. He is also facing a charge of trafficking, which could mean that others may be arrested in relation to this case.
The suspended deputy police commissioner, who was detained on Monday, has made no comment.
The 59-year-old is due to appear in court again on 29 September for a bail application. Prosecutors are expected to oppose bail.
The state has also requested that the court change the prison where Sibiya will be held in the meantime as there are indications of a potential escape plan, national broadcaster SABC is reporting.
The case comes as the police service is in the spotlight at a major public inquiry over allegations of corruption and collusion with criminals.

The inquiry, known as the Madlanga Commission, began last September and has heard accusations that Sibiya received a gift of 20 impalas from an alleged criminal kingpin in exchange for a police contract.
He denied the allegation.

articles.title: High fuel prices force bus operators to cut trips, seek fare hike
articles.summary: Amid the incessant fuel price hikes, several bus operators have been forced to reduce their number of trips to avoid operating at a loss.

blocks.text: Published September 23, 2026 12:42am
Amid the incessant fuel price hikes, several bus operators have been forced to reduce their number of trips to avoid operating at a loss.

In a “24 Oras” report by Oscar Oida on Tuesday, Alex Yague, director of the Provincial Bus Operators Association of the Philippines (PBOAP), shared that several bus terminals now have fewer buses dispatched for trips.
“Lahat ng mga operator ngayon, nagbabawas na ng biyahe,” Yague said.
(All operators right now are reducing their trips.)
“Actually, makikita mo sa mga terminal nila, ‘pag pumasok sa terminal ng bus, napakaraming bus na nakaparada doon na walang biyahe,” he added.
(Actually, you can see it in their terminals—when you go inside a bus terminal, there are so many buses parked there with no scheduled trips.)
To cushion the impact of the recent fuel price hike, PBOAP urged the government to approve the proposed fare increase, stating it would sustain their livelihoods far better than government subsidies.
In March, President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. suspended the scheduled implementation of the fare hike, noting that it would pose a heavy burden on commuters.
“Nakikita namin na dapat nang i-lift na ‘yung suspension [at] ma-implement na ‘yung fare increase para magpatuloy ang serbisyo ng mga provincial buses sa publiko,” Yague said.
(We believe it is time to lift the suspension and implement the fare increase so provincial buses can continue serving the public.)
Charlie Portizo, a 50-year-old jeepney driver, echoed the same call for a fare increase.
Portizo said that while he works hard every day, he takes home very little income for his family.
“Minsan nakaka-P500 pa rin, ‘yun naman ‘yung pinakamalaki pero minsan wala na. ‘Yung diesel namin ‘yung P800 doon na napupunta ‘yung kita namin—sa diesel na lang talaga,” Portiza said.
(Sometimes I still make P500—that’s the highest—but other times, I take home nothing. Around P800 goes toward our diesel—our earnings really just end up going to fuel.)
“Sa totoo lang, sir, ‘di naman namin kailangan talaga ng ayuda. Kailangan namin ngayon, sir, ‘yung taasan man lang ‘yung pamasahe kahit ‘yun man lang. Para kahit papaano maka-survive kami,” he added.
(To be honest, sir, we don't really need subsidies. What we need right now, sir, is at least a fare increase—even just that. So that somehow, we can survive.)
‘Last resort’
The implementation of a fare increase remains the government’s last resort, according to Department of Transportation (DOTr) Secretary Banoy Lopez.
“Sana ho, ang pag-i-impose natin ng fare hike ay maging last resort,” Lopez said.
(Hopefully, imposing a fare hike will be our last resort.)
“‘Pag nagtaas po tayo ng pamasahe, sigurado po makakadagdag din ‘yan sa magiging inflation. Makakadagdag sa presyo rin po ng serbisyo at sa presyo ng mga goods,” he added.
(If we raise fares, it will certainly contribute to inflation. It will also add to the prices of services and basic goods.)
The DOTr added that the government is doing everything it can to assist drivers and operators.

Lopez has ordered the Land Transportation Franchising and Regulatory Board to study the situation and submit recommendations regarding the possibility of a fare hike. —Lyjah Tiffany Bonzo/LDF, GMA News

articles.title: 'I have never felt heat like that' - a survivor on watching 33 cellmates die in Nigeria
articles.summary: The BBC goes inside the prison where prisoners were trapped in stifling, cramped conditions.

blocks.text: Usman Muhammad pauses by the entrance to a tiny Nigerian prison cell and leans his forehead against the wall unable to speak.
The day before he had been trapped inside the stifling room, measuring roughly 6m (19.7ft) by 3m (9.8ft), with more than 50 other prisoners.
Thirty-three of his cellmates died in the cramped conditions in the prison in Minna, the capital of Nigeria's Niger state - and four died later in hospital.
The mass deaths caused an outcry and sparked protests, including attacks on public buildings, as relatives and locals demanded answers.
Federal officials had initially blamed the deaths on a diphtheria outbreak but exactly what happened is now the subject of an investigation.
"I have never felt heat like that in my life. When we touched each other's bodies, it felt like fire burning," Muhammad tells the BBC once he is able to gather his thoughts.

When he was locked inside, there was standing room only amid humidity levels of more than 90%, which in some circumstances can be dangerous to human health as it prevents the natural cooling mechanism of sweat drying on the skin.
The temperature outside was above 25C and the only ventilation came from a small, high-up window.

"One of us fainted and we started knocking at the [cell] door. When [a guard] came we asked him for water. He looked at the guy that fainted and closed the door. That's how they started dying one after the other," Muhammad says.
Like the others who had been detained, the young man, in his 20s, is an artisanal miner, eking out a living searching for precious metals at mine sites.
The federal government has tried to crack down on this alleged illegal activity as it says it costs the country revenue, damages the environment and can be linked to wider criminal activity.
Officers from the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC) had arrested a large group of miners near Minna last Tuesday and Wednesday.
The prisoners were held at its detention centre in the city, but the NSCDC has not shared either the names or the number of those it was holding.

As the hours inside the cell wore on, the heat and dehydration became unbearable and Muhammad says some of the detainees began drinking their own urine and collecting sweat from their bodies to try to stay alive.
He describes seeing people in distress and struggling to breathe.
"People were calling for help, some were already very weak."
But no-one came to help, he and others allege.
"While in the cell, we were shouting and telling them that people were dying," another survivor Adamu Isah told the Reuters news agency.
"We tried to break down the door when they refused to open it… At one point, a security officer came to the door.
"We were shouting and telling him that people were dying, but he said it wasn't his problem if people died."
Finally, on Thursday, the cell door was opened and the guards saw the dead bodies.

The NSCDC has not directly responded to the accusations of neglect and maltreatment but has said that 24 of its personnel are now in custody in connection with the deaths, including its suspended Niger state commandant Suberu Aniviye.
"The people who were killed are not flies. How can this go unlooked? We will get to the bottom of this," Niger state Governor Umaru Bago told the BBC.

articles.title: Skirts take star billing as Prada eschews trousers and dresses in Milan
articles.summary:
Combination of Miuccia Prada with Belgian designer Raf Simons once again spins gold for fashion house

Miuccia Prada’s style formula is simple: begin with a great skirt. Her personal uniform…

blocks.text: Miuccia Prada’s style formula is simple: begin with a great skirt. Her personal uniform is a knee-length skirt, A-line or pleated, most often with a plain sweater and kitten heels. The Prada collection that opened Milan fashion week made a compelling case for her favourite outfit, with a skirt the star of every one of the 63 looks – no dresses, no trousers. It won the room over, so expect to see the personality skirt on a high street near you soon.

For the past six years, Miuccia Prada has shared design duties with Belgian designer Raf Simons, 20 years her junior. The arrangement was considered unusual when announced, but the house of Prada has always had a way of spinning gold from quirky ideas, and it has worked. “She had the idea to focus on skirts this time,” Simons explained before this show. “And I said, why not make it an all-skirt show?”

blocks.caption: Composite: Shutterstock

blocks.text: She prefers skirts to dresses because “they give you room for contrast,” Mrs Prada said. The way I think and feel is complicated, contradictory. If I wear something feminine, I want to wear something masculine too. A dress is all one idea, and we are never just one idea.”

The skirts were mostly A-line and to the knee. A grey wool skirt, severe from the front, flashed a polka-dot violet slip from beneath splits at each side. A lemon skirt was slashed with a ribbon of embroidered black tulle. There were pleated leather skirts, and daisy-printed silk under a layer of sheer gauze. Bare legs and minimal, elegant high heels throughout. Sometimes, the skirts were worn with lace bras, sometimes with a sweater, elsewhere with a shirt. “Whether you want to go to work, or be sexy, or be relaxed with your kids, you can wear the skirt with whatever you choose,” Simons said.

Fashion usually does its talking from the waist up: a slogan T-shirt, a collar and tie, a plunging neckline. Prada’s personality skirt flips the script. “I like my clothes to have ideas,” Mrs Prada explained backstage, “but I don’t want those ideas near my face, because then they get in the way when I am trying to speak. I think of a skirt the way some people think of a T-shirt – a place to express what I think.”

blocks.caption: Composite: Shutterstock

blocks.text: The Prada empire now extends to ownership of one-time rival, Versace. Donatella Versace, who stepped down from her family brand last year, announced on the eve of Milan fashion week that she was launching a new brand. At 71, Versace remains one of the most popular personalities in fashion, with a 12.2 million Instagram following that dwarfs that of most younger designers. She is partnering with California-based Revolve Inc, whose businesses include a joint venture with rapper Cardi B, for an as-yet-unnamed brand that will launch beauty products next year, with fashion further down the line.

There will be no Versace show this Milan fashion week, with new designer Pieter Mulier, newly arrived from Alaïa, preparing for a debut next season instead. Armani, which last week announced the appointment of young designer Dario Vitale to the Emporio Armani brand, positioning him as an eventual successor to the late Giorgio, is also in transition.
after newsletter promotion

This state of flux is unusual for Milan. Power in Italian fashion has long been concentrated in family-run fashion dynasties, creating a quasi-hereditary-peerage system in which the establishment are deeply invested in the status quo. Paris fashion is where audacious moguls place big bets, London is where young talents experiment, but Milan has favoured stability. But with upheaval at several headline houses – the powerful Fendi matriarchy have also stepped back and appointed Maria Grazia Chiuri to lead their brand – that trend is changing.

articles.title: Congressman Gato of Batanes dies, 66
articles.summary: The incumbent congressman from the lone district of Batanes died on Monday due to cardiac arrest. He was 66.

blocks.text: September 23, 2026 | 12:00am
MANILA, Philippines — The incumbent congressman from the lone district of Batanes died on Monday due to cardiac arrest. He was 66.
Rep. Ciriaco Gato Jr., a doctor who also headed the House committee on health, died while en route to Manila for treatment.
Gato, of the Nationalist People’s Coalition, was Batanes representative since 2019. The NPC, now headed by industrialist Ramon Ang of San Miguel Corp., issued a statement.

“The NPC deeply mourns the passing of Rep. Gato, a valued member of the party, a dedicated public servant, and a physician who devoted his life to caring for others. The NPC extends its deepest sympathies and prayers to his loved ones,” it stated.

“Congressman Gato served the people of Batanes with compassion and unwavering dedication. As a medical doctor and chairperson of the House committee on health, he worked tirelessly to improve the health and well-being of Filipinos,” the party added.

“His life of service will be remembered with gratitude and respect. His loss is deeply felt by the people of Batanes, his colleagues in Congress, the NPC and all whose lives he touched. May Congressman Gato rest in eternal peace,” the NPC said.

Speaker Faustino Dy III expressed his deepest sympathies over the passing of Gato, paying tribute to the physician-lawmaker for a life devoted to public service and the welfare of his fellow Filipinos.
“The entire House of Representatives extends its deepest condolences to the family and loved ones of Congressman Ciriaco Gato,” he said.
Special elections
Meanwhile, the Commission on Elections is eyeing Dec. 19 for the special election in Batanes following Gato’s death, Comelec Chairman George Erwin Garcia said yesterday.
Garcia said the proposal on the schedule for the special election would be submitted to the Comelec next week.
“More or less, the initial date is Dec. 19, if that will be approved,” the Comelec chief said in an interview. — Christine Boton

articles.title: Metro Manila rainwater impounding facilities to cost P4 billion
articles.summary: The five proposed rainwater impounding facilities in Metro Manila can store up to 107,600 cubic meters of rainwater and would require more than P4 billion in funding, according to Executive Secretary…

blocks.text: September 23, 2026 | 12:00am
The Office of the Executive Secretayr (OES) on Sept. 22, 2026
Photo from OES

MANILA, Philippines — The five proposed rainwater impounding facilities in Metro Manila can store up to 107,600 cubic meters of rainwater and would require more than P4 billion in funding, according to Executive Secretary Ralph Recto.

The facilities to be administered by the Metropolitan Manila Development Authority (MMDA) form part of ongoing measures to enhance flood mitigation and boost the capital region’s capacity to manage heavy rainfall.

“These impounding facilities will give Metro Manila additional capacity to catch and temporarily store large volumes of rainwater instead of allowing them to immediately overwhelm our drainage systems and flood our communities,” Recto said in a statement.
“When completed, these projects will help protect homes, schools, businesses and public infrastructure, especially during heavy rainfall and high tide,” he added.
The projects will be situated at Camp Aguinaldo, Miriam College, Remedios Circle, Rajah Sulayman Park and the ASEAN Garden at the Cultural Center of the Philippines Complex along Vito Cruz.

“Combined, the five facilities are designed to store up to 107,600 cubic meters of rainwater, providing additional flood water retention capacity in densely populated and flood-prone sections of Metro Manila,” Recto’s office said.
“The five projects have a combined indicative cost of about P4.05 billion, subject to the applicable government review, approval, budgeting and procurement processes,” it added.

The funding for the facilities is proposed under the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management-Disaster Rehabilitation and Reconstruction Assistance Program. MMDA Chairman Romando Artes has submitted documents covering four of the proposed projects to Marcos through Recto’s office and the budget department.

The Camp Aguinaldo facility can cover a 172-hectare catchment area and store up to 50,000 cubic meters of water, while the proposed project at Miriam College will have a 30,000-cubic-meter capacity and serve a 170-hectare catchment area.

The Remedios Circle and Rajah Sulayman Park facilities will have storage capacities of 10,000 cubic meters and 8,000 cubic meters, respectively. Each will serve a 94-hectare catchment area. The flood mitigation project at the ASEAN Garden has a planned capacity of 9,600 cubic meters and can cover a 60-hectare catchment area.
The five projects are among the 39 priority sites for rainwater catchment structures designed to ease the flooding problem in Metro Manila. — Josiah Antonio

articles.title: Philippines developing options on vessel ramming by China
articles.summary: The Philippines is “developing options” to address the ramming of a Bureau of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources vessel by a China Coast Guard ship last Friday off Palawan, Defense Secretary…

blocks.text: September 23, 2026 | 12:00am

MANILA, Philippines — The Philippines is “developing options” to address the ramming of a Bureau of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources (BFAR) vessel by a China Coast Guard (CCG) ship last Friday off Palawan, Defense Secretary Gilbert Teodoro said.

“This definitely needs to be addressed and we’ll be talking with the National Security Adviser and the National Maritime Council,” Teodoro said in an interview on the sidelines of the ASEAN Defense Ministers’ Meeting-Plus Experts’ Working Group on Maritime Security’s Joint Cooperative Activity and Future Leaders’ Program in Olongapo City, Zambales on Monday.
“This is an unarmed vessel, a BFAR vessel. There’s no rhyme, no reason,” he said, referring to the BRP Datu Magat Salamat.

“It’s not merely a violation of maritime rules and regulations, but a criminal act by Chinese Coast Guard. So, we will be addressing that. I’m not going to talk about specifics now, but definitely… our personnel are already developing options for addressing this,” he said.
Asked about some Filipinos defending the CCG’s action against the BFAR vessel, Teodoro said “that is not acceptable, and a betrayal of the Republic of the Philippines.”

In an interview with “Storycon” on One News, Philippine Coast Guard spokesman for the West Philippine Sea Rear Admiral Jay Tarriela said it was the first recorded case of a Chinese ship deliberately ramming an unarmed civilian Philippine vessel.

“This is the first time that we have documented a China Coast Guard vessel aggressively ramming a government vessel from the Philippines that is unarmed, civilian and conducting a humanitarian mission,” Tarriela said.

“It is only 54 nautical miles from Palawan. That is what is surprising about this particular incident,” he said. “They were really caught by surprise. They were not prepared for this intentional ramming.”
He said it would be illogical for the smaller BFAR vessel to intentionally put itself in the path of a much larger Chinese ship.
“I do not think that vessel would intentionally ram itself because its ship is small compared with the Chinese vessel. It would sink,” he said.
Tarriela said he is not authorized to disclose details of any proposed government response but stressed he is in favor of strengthening the country’s maritime capabilities.
“What we need are more Coast Guard assets and more BFAR assets,” he said.
‘China wants new world media order’

In its latest “Propaganda Monitor” released on Monday, the Reporters Without Borders (RSF) meanwhile has warned of China’s worldwide campaign to shape the media to advance its political and economic interests.
The RSF said Chinese leader Xi Jinping has pursued since 2013 a “new world media order” designed to promote Beijing’s narrative while suppressing reporting that challenges the Chinese government.
The group says the campaign uses everything from media partnerships and foreign-language broadcasting to pursue its goals.

The RSF cited Beijing’s content-sharing deals with foreign broadcasters, funding and equipment for local newsrooms, recruitment of diaspora media, government-backed journalist training and fully funded trips to China.
It also pointed to Chinese embassies’ alleged efforts to discredit or intimidate journalists investigating Beijing’s influence – including cases in the Philippines.

The report also highlights the expanding role of Chinese state media like CGTN and Xinhua which operate in 160 countries. Chinese state-linked institutions, meanwhile, increasingly court YouTubers, TikTok creators and other influencers to reach younger audiences.

Beijing has also targeted independent and diaspora journalists overseas, including those in Uyghur as well as Hong Kong journalists based in the United States and the United Kingdom. With its arrest and detention of 120 news professionals, China can be considered the world’s leading jailer of journalists, according to RSF.

It also warned that China’s information strategy increasingly intersects with other authoritarian governments. Chinese state media organizations such as CGTN, for instance, have amplified material from Russian state outlets including RT and Sputnik, including coverage surrounding Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine. Such cooperation could help authoritarian governments expand their influence over the global information environment, according to RSF. — Mark Ernest Villeza, Artemio Dumlao

articles.title: House OKs P785.2 million OVP budget for 2027
articles.summary: The proposed P785.2-million 2027 budget of the Office of Vice President – which is 11.7 percent lower than this year’s P889.2 million allotment – breezed through House plenary…

blocks.text: September 23, 2026 | 12:00am

Office of the Vice President Undersecretary Zuleika Lopez (3rd from left), also the chief of staff of Vice President Sara Z. Duterte, attends the budget hearing of the House of Representatives Committee on Appropriations on Sept. 2, 2026.
PNA photo by Joan Bondoc

MANILA, Philippines — The proposed P785.2-million 2027 budget of the Office of Vice President – which is 11.7 percent lower than this year’s P889.2 million allotment – breezed through House plenary deliberations without any interpellations yesterday.

OVP assistant chief of staff Lemuel Ortonio represented the agency before lawmakers, after his boss, chief of staff Zuleika Lopez submitted a medical certificate asking to be excused from the deliberations.

“We don’t want anything unwelcome to crop up... They were already asking questions during the briefing. It’s just the same. There’s nothing to worry about,” House appropriations committee vice chair and Palawan Rep. Jose Alvarez said during yesterday’s budget hearing.
Alvarez expressed belief that the matter has nothing to do with the ongoing impeachment proceedings against Vice President Sara Duterte.
“We will not look into whether or not she is impeached. The budget is the budget,” he noted. — Evelyn Macairan

articles.title: P27.4 billion extra MAIFIP fund to benefit 5 million families
articles.summary: An estimated five million families will benefit from the additional P27.41-billion funding allocated for the Medical Assistance to Indigent and Financially Incapacitated Patients or MAIFIP program,…

blocks.text: September 23, 2026 | 12:00am
Undated photo of medical equipment in a hospital.
The Philippine STAR / Miguel De Guzman

MANILA, Philippines — An estimated five million families will benefit from the additional P27.41-billion funding allocated for the Medical Assistance to Indigent and Financially Incapacitated Patients or MAIFIP program, according to the Department of Health (DOH).
The current beneficiaries of the program stand at five million families, Health Secretary Edwin Mercado said yesterday.

“Based on our estimate, with the additional funds given, that would also be the number of families and patients we’ll be able to assist,” Mercado said during an interview with the Bagong Pilipinas Ngayon program.

The DOH chief said that bulk or 70 percent of this P27.41 billion, which is equivalent to P19.145 billion, will be used by centers for health development (CHDs), particularly by local government units (LGUs) and private hospitals under these CHDs.

“This amount can be used in emergency as well as catastrophic cases wherein medical expenses are already too high and PhilHealth coverage is not enough. Though we still recommend for the patient to use PhilHealth first and in our order of billing, you can get a discount depending if one falls under the senior citizen or person with disability category,” explained Mercado.

Meanwhile, the remaining amount of the MAIFIP budget was divided among DOH hospitals in Manila (P4.35 billion), GOCC specialty hospitals including the Lung Center, National Kidney and Transplant Institute, Philippine Children’s Medical Center and Philippine Heart Center (P2.9 billion), UP-Philippine General Hospital (P950 million), and drug abuse treatment and rehabilitation center (P52 million).

Over 70 medical and health care groups have called for the abolition of MAIFIP, calling it a medical pork barrel. The groups said the amount for the politicized health ayuda should instead be given to the Philippine Health Insurance Corp. for expanded PhilHealth services.

articles.title: Government OKs P2.48 billion project to upgrade national ID system
articles.summary: The government has approved a P2.48-billion public-private partnership project to further develop and enhance the national identification system, the Philippine Statistics Authority said yesterday.

blocks.text: September 23, 2026 | 12:00am

A man gets his eyes scanned as part of the registration for his national ID at a Philippine Statistics Authority booth at the Quezon Memorial Circle in Quezon City, in this file photo from September 2024.
Miguel De Guzman

MANILA, Philippines — The government has approved a P2.48-billion public-private partnership project to further develop and enhance the national identification system, the Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA) said yesterday.

The Philippine Digital National Identity (PDNI) project secured clearance from the Investment Coordination Committee-Cabinet Committee, chaired by the Department of Finance and co-chaired by the Department of Economy, Planning and Development.
With the approval, the project will move to the procurement stage, where a competitive challenge will be conducted to allow other firms to submit offers for the project.

The competitive challenge is required because the PDNI is an unsolicited proposal from Unisys Public Sector Services Corp., the project’s original proponent. The government will invite competing offers until the fourth quarter of this year, with Unisys retaining the right to match the best offer.
The project will be implemented through a build-transfer-operate arrangement and will cover the upgrade, operation and maintenance of the national ID system.

It will include registration, card production, authentication services, technical onboarding and integration of private-sector relying parties, as well as the operation of the national ID system’s key information and communications technology infrastructure.
The project will have a 20-year concession following a six-month transition period.
Established in 2018 under the Philippine Identification System Act, the national ID aims to provide a single national identification system for all citizens and residents of the country.
Its implementation, however, has faced challenges, including delays in the rollout of physical ID cards.
In 2024, the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas terminated its contract with All Card Inc. for failing to fulfill its commitments to supply national ID cards.

The PSA earlier said the government would deliver the physical cards as required under the law, while the printed electronic Philippine ID and digital national ID remain valid forms of identification.

articles.title: 33% expect economy to improve in a year – SWS
articles.summary: Three in every 10 Filipinos expect the Philippine economy to improve in the next 12 months, according to a new survey by Social Weather Stations.

blocks.text: September 23, 2026 | 12:00am
Shoppers flock to Divisoria in Manila during the holiday break on June17, 2024.
STAR / Ryan Baldemor
MANILA, Philippines — Three in every 10 Filipinos expect the Philippine economy to improve in the next 12 months, according to a new survey by Social Weather Stations (SWS).
The poll, conducted from June 20 to 29, found that 33 percent of the respondents expect the country’s economy to improve within a year.
Thirty-two percent said it will stay the same, while 24 percent said it will worsen. The remaining 11 percent did not give an answer.
The latest survey resulted in a “net economic optimism” score of +10, a 24-point improvement from a low -14 (25 percent optimists, 39 percent pessimists) obtained in a similar survey in March.
The “net economic optimism” is the rounded off difference between those who said their economy will improve and those who said that it will worsen in the next 12 months.
The latest survey showed that net economic optimism improved across all areas, although it remained at negative level among those in Metro Manila.
It was highest among those in balance Luzon at +18 (from -13), followed by those in the Visayas at +6 (from -16), Mindanao at +4 (from -8) and Metro Manila at -6 (from -30).
The SWS survey had 1,200 respondents and a margin of error of plus/minus three percent.

articles.title: Philippines-EU free trade agreement seen next year
articles.summary: The Philippines and the European Union are expected to sign a free trade agreement next year after the conclusion of negotiations.

blocks.text: September 23, 2026 | 12:00am
MANILA, Philippines — The Philippines and the European Union are expected to sign a free trade agreement (FTA) next year after the conclusion of negotiations.

“We just agreed on a EU-Philippine trade deal!” European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said on X yesterday after meeting with President Marcos. “This comes just three years after my visit to Manila to relaunch the negotiations,” she added.
Trade Secretary Cristina Roque and European Commissioner for Trade and Economic Security Maros Sefcovic also announced the development in a joint statement.
“It is essentially concluded,” EU Ambassador Massimo Santoro told reporters covering the ASEAN-EU Business Summit, referring to the trade deal.
He said there is still some work to be finalized on residual elements and the agreement would need to go through legal scrubbing to make it ready for a formal launch.
Roque and Sefcovic said that the FTA is expected to create new opportunities for micro, small and medium enterprises, as well as farmers, manufacturers and consumers on both sides.
The deal is also expected to bring more investment and create more jobs.
In addition, it will support the parties’ shared priorities on sustainable development and the clean and digital transitions.
President Marcos described the conclusions of the free trade talks as an “important milestone” as he vowed to ensure that the opportunities arising from it will benefit Filipinos.

“This is an important milestone in our strong partnership with the European Union and our shared commitment to open and fair trade. The agreement will bring more opportunities for business and investment, create more jobs and support stronger and more diversified supply chains,” Marcos said in a statement hours after his phone call with von der Leyen.

“We will work to ensure that these opportunities reach our Filipino farmers, manufacturers, consumers and MSMEs (micro, small and medium enterprises), while opening new possibilities for the Philippines in AI (artificial intelligence), digital technologies and other important sectors,” he added.
Amid geopolitical and geoeconomic challenges, the FTA is expected to diversify supply chains and provide fair and predictable rules.
After the signing, the FTA will have to be ratified by the Philippine government and European Parliament.

Negotiations for the Philippines-EU FTA were launched in 2015, followed by two rounds, before being put on hold amid the EU’s concerns over the war on drugs waged by the Duterte administration. In 2024, the Philippines and EU agreed to resume FTA negotiations.
Santoro said the parties are aiming to have the FTA in force before the EU Generalized Scheme of Preferences Plus (GSP+) expires by end-2027.
“We wish to be quick in putting this into force,” he said. The Philippines is a beneficiary of the GSP+, which allows the duty-free entry of 6,274 products to the EU.
“The FTA is much more encompassing than the GSP+,” Santoro said.
Predictable trade foundation
European Chamber of Commerce of the Philippines president Diana Edralin said that the FTA provides a predictable foundation for trade and development between the Philippines and EU.
“We strongly urge legislators and political leaders from both the Philippines and the EU to demonstrate swift, decisive commitment to the ratification process,” she said.

“Ensuring an expedited legislative approval in both the Philippine Congress and the European Parliament will allow our business communities, workforce and consumers to realize the full economic dividends of this historic pact without delay,” she added.
German-Philippine Chamber of Commerce and Industry president Christian Scheld said that German businesses are ready to turn the FTA into investments and jobs in the Philippines.
“GPCCI looks forward on its official documentation and ratification well ahead of the expiry of GSP+ in 2027, so that Philippine exporters face no gap in market access,” he said.
For Philippine Chamber of Commerce and Industry president Ferdinand Ferrer, the conclusion of the Philippines-EU FTA reinforces the country’s growing integration into the global economy.

“The business community must now position itself to fully maximize the opportunities that this comprehensive agreement will bring. This FTA has the potential to unlock new growth areas for Philippine enterprises, particularly small and medium-sized enterprises seeking to expand their presence in international markets,” he said.
Philippine Exporters Confederation Inc. president Sergio Ortiz-Luis Jr. said that the development is welcome news for Philippine exporters.

“The EU is a major and high-value market, and an FTA can give our exporters greater market access, more predictable trading conditions, and a stronger platform for expanding Philippine products and services in Europe,” he said.
Federation of Philippine Industries chair Elizabeth Lee said that the Philippines-EU FTA could help position the country as a resilient sourcing and production hub for European firms.
“The real prize is not just market access. It is attracting the investments that create factories, transfer technology and generate quality jobs for Filipinos,” she said.
Last year, the EU was the Philippines’ fourth largest trading partner with trade in goods amounting to 17.6 billion euros ($20.2 billion).

“We strongly believe a regional deal would provide a competitive edge for European and Southeast Asian companies alike, bringing trade and investment to a level that reflects the scale and strategic importance of the ASEAN-EU relationship,” EU-ASEAN Business Council chair Jens Ruebbert said.
The EU has FTAs with Singapore and Vietnam, and finalized the negotiations for its FTA with Indonesia in September last year. — Pia Lee-Brago, Alexis Romero

articles.title: Cyber patrols to be intensified vs online ‘grooming’
articles.summary: Cyber patrols will be enhanced to detect online “grooming,” recruitment and other activities exposing minors to violence or criminal behavior, according to the National Capital Region…

blocks.text: September 23, 2026 | 12:00am

MANILA, Philippines — Cyber patrols will be enhanced to detect online “grooming,” recruitment and other activities exposing minors to violence or criminal behavior, according to the National Capital Region Police Office.

The NCRPO has directed the regional anti-cybercrime unit to monitor online communities, threats, recruitments, calls for violence, games and other digital platforms that may expose minors to excessive violence or encourage dangerous activities.
Police operations will not target legitimate online gaming or the youth’s usage of technology, but the misuse of digital platforms to manipulate or recruit minors.
School shootings have occurred in Tacloban, Zamboanga and South Cotabato in the last three months.
The NCRPO urged parents, guardians and teachers to monitor children’s online activities, including their private chats, gaming communities and social media groups.
“Know what your children are watching, who they are communicating with and what online communities they are joining,” NCRPO officer-in-charge Brig. Gen. Christopher Abrahano said yesterday.
“Our objective is prevention. We want to detect threats before they become real-world violence,” he added.
People should not circulate videos, photos, threats or other sensitive material related to violent incidents, the NCRPO stressed.

Police will coordinate with the Department of Education, Cybercrime Investigation and Coordinating Center (CICC), schools, parents and other agencies to prevent online exploitation and other cyber-enabled threats.
Reddit, Discord reps
The CICC has issued a 24-hour ultimatum to online forum Reddit and messaging platform Discord to designate representatives and establish a physical presence in the Philippines.

Threatening a nationwide ban for noncompliance, the CICC clarified: “We are not asking platforms to police the internet for the government, but to be reachable, accountable and responsive when activities on their platforms put Filipino children and communities at risk.”
Reddit and Discord should join an integrated inter-agency framework to dismantle networks creating, soliciting, distributing and monetizing online child abuse and its materials, the CICC said.

To bolster compliance, the CICC has requested the Department of Foreign Affairs to facilitate high-level diplomatic and coordination meetings with Reddit, Discord, Meta and other social media networks operating in the country.
Palace open to Big Tech congressional franchise
Malacañang is open to a bill requiring social media firms to obtain a congressional franchise and subject them to Philippine laws.
Rep. David Suarez has filed a bill classifying online social networks as public services that must secure a franchise from legislature.

“That (bill) is being discussed and that is what the Department of Information and Communications Technology proposes, so that as much as possible, we can have jurisdiction and authority over these social media platforms. So that is a good proposal,” Palace press officer Claire Castro said yesterday.

Under House Bill 4786, the DICT and National Telecommunications Commission will have regulatory and oversight functions over social media entities, which will be required to have a local presence in the country.
Castro refuted Vice President Sara Duterte’s statement blaming the Marcos administration for the school shootings.

“It is not true that the government is not doing anything… We cannot force someone to understand the situation if he or she is unwilling to understand or just can’t understand,” Castro said. — Rainier Allan Ronda, Alexis Romero, Evelyn Macairan

articles.title: Sara holds no interest in GenCorp – Baste
articles.summary: Vice President Sara Duterte has neither kept nor maintained any interest in GenCorp Industries Inc. since she assumed the post in 2022, Davao City Mayor Sebastian “Baste” Duterte insisted.

blocks.text: September 23, 2026 | 12:00am
Vice President Sara Duterte and her brother, Davao City Acting Mayor Baste Duterte photographed in July 2025 at the inaugural ceremony of new Davao City officials.
Inday Sara Duterte via FB

MANILA, Philippines — Vice President Sara Duterte has neither kept nor maintained any interest in GenCorp Industries Inc. since she assumed the post in 2022, Davao City Mayor Sebastian “Baste” Duterte insisted.

“I, and all other officials and employees of the city government of Davao, never had any knowledge of Vice President Sara Z. Duterte holding an interest in GenCorp Industries Inc.,” the mayor said in a statement released on Monday.
He said neither the names “Sara Zimmerman Duterte” nor “Duterte” appear in GenCorp’s official documents submitted for the transactions, including its Articles of Incorporation.

Duterte, the Vice President’s younger brother, maintained that the city’s transactions with GenCorp Industries were aboveboard. He said claims to the contrary must be supported by verified evidence and reliable documents.
“In every instance, Gencorp Industries Inc. was rigorously evaluated and determined to have submitted the lowest calculated responsive bid or offer.

“Most importantly, in compliance with government procurement laws and administrative issuances, all 19 transactions have been duly processed, reported, and published on the Philippine Government Electronic Procurement System portal,” the mayor said.
He urged the public to be cautious about unverified claims and narratives, which he said could be politically motivated.

“Let us all be vigilant in managing information and not fall prey to deceptive claims and orchestrated narratives engineered solely to serve political motives that suit personal interests and promote disunity,” he said.

“I remain steadfast in my commitment to transparency, fairness and the absolute truth. This statement is issued ahead of any so-called lawful proceedings as I believe that the people, especially the people of the City of Davao, have the right to know,” he said.
The Vice President declared Gencorp Industries as one of her business interests in her statement of assets, liabilities and net worth.
However, Gencorp did not list her as an incorporator or director based on the firm’s General Information Sheet and Audited Financial Statement submitted to the Securities and Exchange Commission.
The Davao City LGU had P33,263,161 worth of transactions with Gencorp Industries Inc., covering 19 contracts, contrary to reports citing around P14.32 million.
The mayor said of the 19 contracts that began in 2022, 13 have been completed while six are ongoing.

He explained that four contracts were awarded through competitive public bidding and 15 contracts were processed through small value procurement, as allowed under procurement rules. — Daphne Galvez, Evelyn Macairan

articles.title: No dividends: Defense argument strengthens prosecution's case --Adiong
articles.summary: “Why did the Vice President declare that all these companies who have not consistently [been] declaring dividends can actually justify the increase of her net worth?" said Rep. Adiong.

blocks.text: VP SARA DUTERTE IMPEACHMENT
Published September 22, 2026 11:17pm

The impeachment defense team’s argument that the law does not mandate the declaration of dividends bolsters the prosecution’s assertion that Vice President Sara Duterte’s increase in net worth cannot be accounted for by the business interests she declared in her SALN, the prosecution panel said.

“That [Corporation Code invoked by the defense] is irrelevant and immaterial. He went through a lot of technical details, processes under the revised corporate law but it does not answer one very basic and simple question: Where did the Vice President get all the money reflected in her SALN?” House prosecution panel spokesperson Zia Adiong of Lanao del Sur said in a press conference.

“And why did the Vice President declare that all these companies who have not consistently [been] declaring dividends can actually justify the increase of her net worth?...It even further strengthened the case of the prosecution na hindi iyon ang source of income niya [that these businesses are not the source of her income],” Adiong added.

Impeachment trial defense counsel Justin Gular on Tuesday defended the absence of declared dividends of 10 businesses linked to Duterte and her husband Manases Carpio, saying the law does not require the declaration of dividends.

Gular invoked Section 42 of the Corporation Code, which states that “the board of directors of a stock corporation may declare dividends out of the unrestricted retained earnings which shall be payable in cash, property, or in stock to all stockholders on the basis of outstanding stock held by them.”

Gular then asked prosecution witness SEC Company Registration and Monitoring Department Director Gerardo del Rosario: “So as a lawyer and as an officer of the SEC, you confirm that just because a corporation has unrestricted retained earnings, it’s not automatically required by law para mag-declare ng dibidendo [to declare dividends]. Tama po ba? [Would that be correct?]”
Del Rosario replied, "Tama po." (That’s correct.)

Later in the day, prosecution witness and Philippine Government Electronic Procurement System (PhilGEPS) Division Chief Rendell Sopeña told the Senate impeachment court that GenCorp. Industries Inc, listed by the Vice President as one of her business interest in her 2024 and 2025 Statement of Assets, Liabilities and Net Worth, won P35 million worth of government contracts when Duterte was Vice President.
Sopeña said that the Philippine Health Insurance Corp. (PhilHealth) Region 11 awarded 33 contracts to GenCorp.
Davao City government, on the other hand, also awarded 15 contracts to GenCorp.
The Overseas Workers Welfare Administration (OWWA) Region 11, for its part, awarded one contract of GenCorp. — BM, GMA News

articles.title: Gums, gingkos and a golden wych elm: voting for Victoria’s tree of the year
articles.summary:
From Carlton to Castlemaine, the National Trust of Victoria competition aims to raise awareness about trees

  • Get our

blocks.text: A decades-old shady eucalyptus, an elm beloved by thousands of commuters, and a type of gingko once thought to be extinct in the wild are among the finalists for Victoria’s tree of the year.
The competition run by the National Trust of Victoria started in 2016 as a way to raise awareness about trees around Victoria and advocate for their protection by celebrating significant trees.

To be eligible, the trees must be listed on the National Trust significant tree register, which it recognises up to 10,000 important trees in Victoria for their cultural, scientific, and historic value.
This year it had more than 40 nominations, which were narrowed down to nine finalists by a panel of 12 experts and arboriculturists.

The executive manager of gardens at the National Trust, Justin Buckley, said the trees nominated for the registry have been there for generations, and the people who nominated them often remember playing under them and climbing them, along with their children.
“It’s not always just the biggest or most impressive tree that wins; it’s often one that has a lot of community support behind it.” Buckley said.
The 2026 finalists are:

blocks.caption: Myrtle beech (Nothofagus cunninghamii) in Apollo Bay. Photograph: Sarah Rees

blocks.text: The famed myrtle beech in Apollo Bay may be the result of two or three trees growing together and visitors are able to wander through the complex structure: a parallel to the web of life they support.

blocks.caption: Flooded gum (Eucalyptus grandis) in Carlton North. Photograph: National Trust

blocks.text: Although flooded gums only naturally grow north of Newcastle, and especially in very wet areas like the Daintree, this specimen most likely planted in the 1960s or 70s in Carlton North is a landmark of pride for the community.

blocks.caption: Californian redwoods (Sequoia semperverens) in Warburton. Photograph: National Trust

blocks.text: These trees were planted as a experiment by the Melbourne Metropolitan Board of Works in the 1930s in order to see if conifers could clean drinking water in a landscape which had been extensively cleared. Growing much taller than any other trees, they offer visitors an awe-inspiring experience.

blocks.caption: Ginkgo (Ginkgo biloba) in Geelong. Photograph: National Trust

blocks.text: The ginkgo was planted in Geelong Botanic Gardens in 1859, and is more than 167 years old. Gingkos, also known as maidenhairs, were thought to be extinct in the wild for many centuries before being revived.
after newsletter promotion

blocks.caption: Indian bean tree (Catalpa bignonioides) in Castlemaine. Photograph: Mount Alexander Shire/National Trust

blocks.text: The Indian bean tree is located in the botanical gardens in Castlemaine. Originally from Central America, the tree is known to herald the season by covering itself in large white flowers in spring and growing a full shady green canopy of large leaves in summer and long seed pods in winter.

blocks.caption: Smooth barked apple myrtle (Angphora costata) in Prahran Photograph: National Trust

blocks.text: This smooth-barked apple myrtle in Prahran is the biggest of its kind in cultivation. Located in the middle of urban Melbourne and surrounded by construction works, there are hopes that architects will let the tree continue to grow for many years to come.

blocks.caption: Canary Island pine (Pinus canariensis) in Ballarat. Photograph: National Trust

blocks.text: Planted by 1867 Jacob Bernstein, a member of Ballarat’s Hebrew community, this Canary Island pine is the second-eldest recorded tree among the finalists and is a recognisable feature in the landscape of Ballarat. Canary Island pines are known for their longevity and ability to survive changes in climate.

blocks.caption: Golden wych elm (Ulmus glabra ‘Lutescens’) in South Yarra Photograph: Jess Hood/National Trust
Bunya pine (Araucaria bidwilii) in Maldon. Photograph: National Trust

blocks.text: The competition is the trust’s most successful advocacy campaign and helps bring awareness to important trees in Victoria, Buckley said.

“In the 40-odd years that we’ve been keeping the significant tree register, they’re potentially under more threat than they ever have been with densification of cities and more housing; we think protection of trees is as important as it’s ever been,” Buckley said.
Voting for the competition closes at midnight, 22 October, with the winner announced on 27 October.

articles.title: Alex Antic’s rise in SA Liberals has coincided with a collapse in the party’s vote. Is there further to fall?
articles.summary:
Election of rightwing senator – once called a ‘vote-losing machine’ – as state president in South Australia takes party further from the centre

  • Get our

blocks.text: Rogue Liberal senator Alex Antic says he will give “back some voice” to party members now that he has been elected as state president in South Australia.
Many of those members are part of “Alex’s Army”, the evangelical and Pentecostal Christians the federal MP recruited into the operational wing of the party.
That has given the rightwinger a huge amount of influence in a state that for years was the scene of turf wars between the conservatives and the moderates.
Over the weekend, Antic beat upper house leader Nicola Centofanti 119 to 73 votes to take the presidency.

The prospect of Antic as president led some to speculate that the federal party might forcibly take over the state branch because of concerns over the senator’s close relationship with One Nation and whether Antic was likely to improve the beleaguered party’s vote.
Pollster Tony Barry, the RedBridge director of corporate affairs and communications, has branded Antic a “vote-losing machine” for the party.
Since his ascendancy, the Liberal party has been smashed at a federal and a state election.

After SA’s March election, the Liberal party was left with just five lower house seats. Moderates are concerned that opposition leader Ashton Hurn’s attempts to turn around the party’s fortunes will be made more difficult if she is constantly asked about Antic’s musings on topics including vaccinations, trans issues and climate change.
On Monday, Antic posted to X that his win was a “great result”.
“It’s proof positive that getting involved in politics can achieve outcomes, grassroots political action as it’s known, people joining up, turning up to vote,” he said.
“And … we’re going to give the members of this party back some voice into the machine”.
It’s not clear how he would deliver on that promise.
The organisational wing of the party “cannot dictate policy”, the party says, “but consults with and advises the parliamentary wing, particularly on the development of longer-term policies”.
However, Antic could use his power to force constitutional change, to pre-select candidates that are ideologically aligned, or to pressure sitting MPs to adopt more rightwing policies.

Trish Worth, a state council delegate and Howard government parliamentary secretary, told the ABC the party “should always be selecting the people with the most experience and loyalty”, and criticised his recent moves to change the No Jab, No Play legislation.
He was the only Coalition senator to vote for that change, but was joined by the four One Nation senators and United Australia Party senator Ralph Babet.
On Monday, state health minister Blair Boyer called on Antic to declare whether he would seek to form a coalition with One Nation.
after newsletter promotion
“The transformation is complete,” Boyer said.
“The South Australian Liberals are now the Temu version of One Nation – just as extreme, just as dangerous, just less genuine.”
One Nation’s SA leader, Cory Bernardi – who was snapped enjoying a beer with Antic earlier this year – welcomed Antic’s win, and said he looked forward to their ongoing “constructive relationship”.
Liberal senator Anne Ruston wished Antic the best, now he had two “enormous” jobs as president and senator.
Antic’s close conservative colleague Tony Pasin told the ABC on Monday the Liberal party and One Nation should “work together to defeat the Australian Labor party”.
Pasin said the advantage of the presidency was “there might be an opportunity for people to look a little closer at what Alex says from time to time”, for example on vaccination.
In June, Antic claimed in the senate that pharmaceutical companies were using the bird flu to push people to get the flu jab.

“These birds are almost like the bell ringing on the pharmaceutical company’s guilt trip, saying: ‘We’re entering the winter season. We’re about to lean on you to get your flu shot, and now we’ve found two birds with the sniffles’”, he said.
Pasin said he agreed with Antic, but that he was merely saying that the flu jab did not protect against bird flu.
Asked whether people in the Liberal party might be “concerned about repercussions” from Antic’s election, Pasin said the party “should be focused on winning elections”.
Antic did not respond to questions by deadline, and said on X that he had “no intention” of dealing much with the media.

articles.title: Autopsy shows Hayden Panettiere died from a drug overdose
articles.summary: The death of the child star - who had fentanyl, Xanax, a muscle relaxant and antipsychotic medication in her system - was ruled an accident.

blocks.text: Child star Hayden Panettiere died from the toxic effects of fentanyl, Xanax and several other drugs in her system, according to an autopsy completed by the Greenville County Coroner's Office in South Carolina.
The coroner's office said Panettiere's death was an accident and that no signs of trauma were discovered that would have contributed to her death.
Panettiere died last month at the age of 36 after she was found unresponsive at a South Carolina residence.
The star of US TV shows Heroes and Nashville had spoken openly about her struggles with substance abuse.
The coroner's office also found methocarbamol - a prescription muscle relaxant - and quetiapine - an antipsychotic medication that is used to treat certain mental health conditions.

items: Drugs at their fingertips, intense pressure: Why child stars fall into addiction

blocks.text: Fentanyl is a synthetic opioid that has killed hundreds of thousands of Americans over the past five years alone.
The coroner's office said emergency responders had "initiated advanced cardiac life support measures; however, resuscitation efforts were unsuccessful".
The US Drug Enforcement Agency (DEA) was reportedly joining the local police department's investigation into the child star's death.

Panettiere's ex-boyfriend, Brian Hickerson - who has admitted to abusing her - and his brother Zack were with Panettiere when emergency services came, according to a police report from the day she died.
Just months before her death, Panettiere published a memoir where she discussed at length her issues with addiction and postpartum depression.
