articles.title: Could we see MMA at the Olympics?
articles.summary: Mixed martial arts has made its debut at the Asian Games this week. It takes the sport closer to the Olympics but there are doubts about the next step, and the influence of the popular and lucrative…

image.caption: MMA has made its debut at the 2026 Asian GamesImage: Dita Alangkara/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: The form of mixed martial arts (MMA) making its debut at the Asian Games looks almost completely distinct from the visceral brawls of the Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC), which have come to define combat sports in recent years.

In order to get a version of the sport into the Games, currently taking place in Nagoya in Japan, adaptations had to be made. The fights take place without the familiar cage, on an open mat and with small boxing-style gloves. While MMA's presence in the Asian Games is significant in itself, it's also a clear effort to get close to Olympic recognition.

"We think without the cage we will have a better alignment with the Olympic values and hopefully recognition from the IOC," Galastein Tan, the director general of Federation of International Mixed Martial Arts (FIMMA), told press agency AP. "It takes time to change a perception. We hope to be able to share that there is a new form of MMA, and this form is more aligned with the Olympics."

FIMMA is not the only body purporting to represent the sport, with the International Mixed Martial Arts (IMMAF) also staking a claim. But Tan, a Chinese billionaire property mogul, is a vice president of the Olympic Council of Asia. This could potentially open doors in a movement which has so far kept MMA at arm's length, with violence levels among its concerns. DW contacted both FIMMA and the IMMAF for comment but received no response.
UFC has outstripped MMA

In the past the UFC, a lucrative MMA-based competition, has also pushed for Olympic recognition. But the growth of that arm of the sport, highlighted by it staging an event on the South Lawn of the White House at the 250th anniversary celebrations of US independence earlier this year, has meant that the aims of a sport that was marginal two decades ago have shifted according to Karim Zidan.

blocks.caption: UFC hosted matches at the White House earlier this yearImage: Kent Nishimura/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: "I don't necessarily think it's that important to MMA. The sport has already found its success on a professional level, which is what the fan base demanded of it," said Zidan, who has written an upcoming book 'The Ultimate Strongmen: MMA and the Rise of the New Authoritarian Right' on the subject.

"The UFC is bigger than it's ever been in terms of the amount of money it's making" added Zidan. "The UFC's growth mainstreamed MMA as a sport, but it also cannibalized it. So there's really not much remaining. Olympic recognition might seem like a badge of honor, but it doesn't amount to much else."

With events for the 2028 Olympics in Los Angeles already set, the earliest MMA could make its bow would be 2032 in Brisbane. But the IOC told AP that "mixed martial arts does not meet ... eligibility criteria" at this point. DW has sought clarification from the IOC on this.
Does MMA have enough appeal for Olympics?
Tan appears to be trying to find a way to change that, citing the sport's popularity. "MMA is popular globally, able to engage fans at a gut level and attract fans at a youth level," he said.
But Zidan argues that its popularity is through the UFC, rather than any grassroots popularity.

"There isn't much of an MMA ecosystem outside of the UFC for me to say there's an entirely different worldview existing in the sport that's demanding this. There are pockets within the sport that enjoy amateur MMA and are operating within it, but I don't think it's a significant part of the fan base at all," Zidan said.

"I'm not particularly convinced that this is a turning point or a significant moment for mixed martial arts, honestly. I think the sport has suffered tremendously under the burden and the weight of the UFC over the past decade."
Senegal gears up for Youth Olympic Games
UFC's links with the Trump administration are deep and clear, with UFC president Dana White also speaking at the Republican convention in 2024.

But Zidan also pointed to the IMMAF's link up with Brave Combat Federation, a Bahraini organization headed by Khalid bin Hamad Al Khalifa, a son of King of Bahrain, Hamad bin Isa Al Khalifa. A 2025 Amnesty International Report said Bahrain continued to "to suppress the rights to freedom of expression, association and peaceful assembly, including through arbitrary detention and prosecutions."
Authoritarian links remain for MMA
Such links with authoritarian governments have become, Zidan added, fairly commonplace in the sport.

"They've already had associations with authoritarian regimes in the past and it's very likely that relationship will build. If this [the Asian Games and potential Olympic acceptance] means that we will now have more amateur MMA events being hosted around the world in youth championships, it's very likely that authoritarian regimes will jump on that."

The challenge for FIMMA, who appear to want to take MMA in the Olympic direction and away from UFC and its associations, is to make the sport more "normal" and less about spectacle, FIMMA's vice president Alex Engelhardt told AP.
"It's very challenging in the sense that the whole mindset in the sport is so focused on promotions," he said.
Even if that can change, and sport's debut at the Asian Games adds some legitimacy, the Olympics still seem some way off.

articles.title: House approves P975.96B budget for DepEd in 2027
articles.summary: The House of Representatives approved on Tuesday the proposed P975.96-billion budget of the Department of Education (DepEd) for fiscal year 2027.

blocks.text: Published September 22, 2026 8:02pm
The House of Representatives approved on Tuesday the proposed P975.96-billion budget of the Department of Education (DepEd) for fiscal year 2027.
This allocation for the Education Department represents 13.55% of the proposed national budget for 2027, according to Appropriations Committee Vice Chair Rep. Maria Carmen Zamora.
“Once again, this single largest allocation of any department in the government as part of the education sector, consistent with the mandate of the Constitution,” Zamora said.
“It affirms that this house and this admin continue to treat education not as an expense but as the nation's most important investment,” she added.
Under DepEd’s budget, the highlighted major items include the School-Based Feeding Program (SBFP), government assistance and subsidies, and teacher promotions.
The SBFP was allocated P11.4 billion, eyed to provide public school learners with nutritious meals, addressing malnutrition while improving classroom attendance.

ACT Teachers Party-list Representative Antonio Tinio highlighted a 55% slash to the feeding program’s funding, while Gabriela Party-list Representative Sarah Elago pointed out a P14-billion overall drop in its allocation.

When asked how the budget cut would impact operations, Zamora explained that the feeding program’s duration will be trimmed from 180 days to 120 days and restricted primarily to kindergarten students.

“This will affect the number of days in the implementation, so instead na nasa 180 days magiging 120 days na lang’ yung implementation and will be limited only for kindergarten learners in terms of universal coverage,” Zamora said.

(This will affect the number of days in the implementation, so instead of 180 days, the implementation will be reduced to 120 days and will be limited only to kindergarten learners in terms of universal coverage.)
In 2026, the SBFP received a P25.7-billion budget. Elago urged fellow lawmakers to restore the program’s funding to its 2026 level to prevent a reduction in services.

“Sinusuportahan ng representasyon na ito ang pagre-restore ng pondo para dito sa School-Based Feeding Program doon sa level niya sa 2-26 para mamentena po natin kung ano na currently yung ating binibigay na napakahalagang serbisyo sa mga learners,” Elago said.
(This representation supports the restoration of funds for the School-Based Feeding Program to its 2026 level so we can maintain the essential services we currently provide to our learners.)
Among other key allocations, DepEd’s government assistance and subsidies received P38.12 billion.
Meanwhile, P12.09 billion was set aside to support the expanded career progression program, paving the way for the promotion and professional advancement of qualified public school teachers.
DepEd remains the largest beneficiary in the proposed 2027 budget, according to the Department of Budget and Management.
In 2026, the agency received a P1.015-trillion budget, marking the highest allocation in its history.
This budget approval by the lower chamber does not finalize DepEd’s 2027 funding.

The budget will still undergo scrutiny during the bicameral conference committee between the House and Senate, where the final version of the General Appropriations Act will be reconciled and finalized. —NB, GMA News

articles.title: DepEd: Lack of qualified applicants leaves 'hard-to-fill' posts vacant
articles.summary: Aside from teaching positions that the Department of Education (DepEd) has yet to fill, the agency said some “hard-to-fill” posts remain vacant due to several factors, including a lack of qualified…

blocks.text: The Department of Education (DepEd) said some “hard-to-fill” positions in the agency remain vacant due to a lack of qualified applicants and other factors.

“The reasons behind the delays in filling up some of these plantilla positions are attributed to several factors. One of these is that there are hard-to-fill positions, which include the non-teaching positions,” House Committee on Appropriations Vice Chair and Davao De Oro Rep. Maria Carmen Zamora said on Tuesday.
Zamora made the statement while defending the department’s proposed 2027 budget during plenary debates in the House of Representatives.
According to Zamora, among these hard-to-fill positions are guidance counselors, attorneys, and special education and science teachers,

“There are also factors like waiving of beneficiaries under special hiring guidelines, and there are instances where there are a lack of qualified applicants for appropriate specializations,” she said.
Previously, during a House of Representatives budget deliberation on DepEd’s proposed 2027 budget, the agency received zero allocation for the hiring of new teachers in the next fiscal year.

ACT Teachers Party-list Representative Antonio Tinio asked DepEd whether it would still refrain from requesting new plantilla items, given the agency’s previous report of a shortage of more than 14,000 teachers.
In response, Zamora explained that the department’s hiring process remains ongoing and will continue until December this year.

“The Department is on its continuous hiring process until next year, because the allocation given to the department from the GAA (General Appropriations Act) 2026 is still being implemented starting this year,” Zamora said.
“...Therefore, there’s no such thing that we stopped hiring. We are still hiring as we speak until December of this year,” she added.
Zamora said the 2026 GAA created a total of 31,428 positions, of which 22,711 had been filled and 8,688 remained vacant as of June 30, 2026.
The number of vacant teaching positions under DepEd currently stands at more than 20,000, factoring in an additional 12,646 unfilled positions carried over from previous years, according to Zamora.
Out-of-pocket expenses
The House on Tuesday approved the proposed P975.96-billion budget of DepEd for 2027.
Several lawmakers flagged decreases in allocations for some line items, including a minimal increase in the department’s Maintenance and Other Operating Expenses (MOOE).
MOOE refers to funds allocated for the day-to-day operating expenses of the department, including individual public schools across the country.
Tinio pointed out that the minimal MOOE increase would be outpaced by the country’s inflation rate, providing little relief amid rising prices.
“Why is the proposed increase in the NEP and the General Appropriations Bill so small, not even reaching one percent?” Tinio said in Filipino.
“That means, in effect, this is a decrease because it is way below even the current inflation rate today. So, it did not even keep pace with it,” he added.
Data presented before the House showed the following increases in school operations budgets compared with the 2026 GAA:

items: Elementary (Kinder to Grade 6) — 0.11%
Junior High School (Grades 7 to 10) — 0.38%
Senior High School (Grades 11 to 12) — 0.33%

blocks.text: Tinio said the low MOOE allocation remains a primary complaint among schools, with teachers often forced to pay out of pocket for classroom and school needs.
“If we ask the schools, that is one of the basic complaints. At the school level, the MOOE is insufficient, right?” Tinio said.
“Generating operating expenses is always a problem, and it is often left to teachers to cover out of their own pockets,” he added.

For its part, Zamora said DepEd follows a formula in determining allocations for each school, adding that the department implemented a policy adjustment last year to refine these allocations based on various factors.
“In line with the setting of the formula in terms of allocation of MOOE for schools, we take note… Very valid observation,” Zamora said.
Tinio proposed that roughly P3 billion be added to the MOOE allocation to help schools keep pace with inflation. — MCG, GMA News

articles.title: Palace on Sara Duterte's business ties: No one is above the law
articles.summary: Malacañang asserted Tuesday that no one is above the law, issuing the statement following testimonies from an official of the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) regarding the business interests…

blocks.text: Published September 22, 2026 7:52pm Updated September 23, 2026 12:30am

Malacañang asserted Tuesday that no one is above the law, issuing the statement following testimonies from an official of the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) regarding the business interests of Vice President Sara Duterte.

This developed after Gerardo del Rosario, director of the SEC Company Registration and Monitoring Department, testified at Duterte's impeachment trial that the vice president remained on the Board of Directors of Metro City Chow Foods Corporation until 2025, well after she was elected to the post, despite a constitutional prohibition.

"May batas po. Maliwanag ang batas. So, kung ano po iyong nasa batas iyon lang dapat po ang sundin, iyon ang dapat na ipatupad at hindi po kinakailangan na ang isang tao ay maging above the law," Castro said in a press briefing.
(There is a law. The law is clear. So whatever is in the law, that should be followed, that should be what is implemented, so there is no need for one person to be above the law.)
"So, hindi po dapat pinapairal iyong salitang impunity. So, kung ano lang po iyong sa batas dapat tuparin," Castro said.
(So the word impunity should not be common. Whatever is in the law should be what is implemented.)

Also during the impeachment trial on Monday, Del Rosario testified on the corporate records of 18 firms which either the vice president or her husband, lawyer Manases Carpio, allegedly owns or has business interests in.
Del Rosario continued his testimony on Tuesday, wherein he affirmed that ownership of shares is evidence of participation in a business.
Asked about Senator-Judge Raffy Tulfo's question asking why Duterte was not legally advised about her business dealings, Castro declined to comment further.
"Hindi na po kami magkokomento diyan, si VP Sara naman ay malaki na at hindi na dapat binibigyan ng anumang advice, alam niya na po ang kanyang ginagawa," Castro said.
(We will not comment on that, VP Sara is grown and does not need advice, she knows what she is doing.)
Cross examination
Duterte’s defense indicated that the records presented by the SEC did not necessarily prove any wrongdoing, casting doubt on the veracity of the documents.
During its cross-examination, defense counsel Justin Nicol Gular asked about the unsigned and unsealed SEC audit summaries of Duterte’s businesses.

“And you confirm that both these summaries that your office supposedly prepared are also unsigned or walang perma po ng kahit sinuman? Tama po ba?” Gular asked the witness, SEC officer Gerardo del Rosario. (And you confirm that both these summaries that your office supposedly prepared are also unsigned and there is no signature from anyone.)
Del Rosario answered in the affirmative.
The defense counsel also asked the SEC witness if he could not confirm that Duterte received anything.
“You cannot confirm whether, based on the net income report, na may natanggap ang bise presidente diyan?” Gular del Rosario.
(You cannot confirm whether, based on the net income report, that the vice president received anything there?)
Del Rosario again answered in the affirmative. —VDV/NB, GMA News

articles.title: After Rappler report, more Gencorp contracts with Davao City Hall confirmed
articles.summary: PhilGEPS and Davao City Mayor Sebastian Duterte separately confirm that Gencorp's contracts with Davao City Hall are worth more than twice the amount previously reported

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines – A Philippine Government Electronic Procurement System (PhilGEPS) official, and even Davao City Mayor Sebastian Duterte, confirmed that the company linked to Vice President Sara Duterte won more contracts than initially and exclusively reported by Rappler.

PhilGEPS division chief Rendell Sopeña told the impeachment court on Tuesday, September 22, that according to its database, Gencorp Industries bagged P34.2 million in projects with the Davao City government, more than twice the P14.3 million in contracts previously identified by Rappler in its September 15 report.

The younger Duterte said in a press release earlier Tuesday that Gencorp has P33.2 million in contracts with Davao City Hall since 2022, coinciding with the time his older sister became vice president and he assumed the mayorship of their hometown.

The Davao City mayor’s confirmatory statement came with a claim that he did not have knowledge of his sister’s ties to Gencorp, and an assertion that all of city hall’s deals with Gencorp were aboveboard.
“Any claim otherwise shall be duly supported with verified evidence and reliable documents,” Mayor Duterte said.
The Vice President’s name is not in any Securities and Exchange Commission filing of Gencorp, but she claimed to be its stockholder in her Statement of Assets, Liabilities, and Net Worth.
The prosecution believes the findings strengthen its case of unexplained wealth against the Vice President, which it said is a betrayal of public trust and a culpable violation of the Constitution.

blocks.caption: After Rappler report, more Gencorp contracts with Davao City Hall confirmed

blocks.text: “This is where the conflict of interest comes in. Given the blood relationship between the local chief executive, Mayor Baste, and one of Gencorp’s shareholders, the company won a contract with city hall. On that aspect, there was a violation,” prosecution spokesman Zia Adiong said. “The Vice President should have divested.”
The 1987 Constitution explicitly prohibits the Vice President from maintaining business interests while in office.

articles.title: What is the White House press pool and why is it in a row with Trump?
articles.summary: The White House press pool is at the centre of a major row between President Donald Trump and TV networks. What is it?

blocks.text: Image source, EPA
A network boycott affected live TV coverage of Trump's ribbon-cutting event at the White House
When Donald Trump unveiled a helipad at the White House on Monday, his remarks were barely audible in live footage of the event.
This was due to a row over an institution that rarely makes the news – the White House Press pool.
Yet it is at the heart of relations between the US president and the media, and this dispute could have constitutional implications.
Coverage of upcoming presidential engagements, which include the UN General Assembly in New York, could be affected.
What is the White House press pool?
It is a group of news organisations that combine resources to follow presidents wherever they are - in the Oval Office, at state dinners, on Air Force One or on holiday.
There are separate pools for TV, photographers and print and radio outlets, as well as a "new media" category.

Material from the TV pool feed is shared between its members - CNN, ABC, CBS, Fox News and NBC - to save on costs and space. The pool is always on standby in case an event requires the president to speak to the nation.

The latest row began on Friday, when Trump said he was banning three outlets - CNN, Politico and MS NOW - from the White House, accusing them of spreading "fake news" and "fictions and lies" about his team.
A day later, reporters from those organisations found that their entry badges to the White House had been disabled.
On Monday, all the major US TV networks decided to pull out of White House pool duties - in effect boycotting presidential events.

That afternoon came the first test of this post-pool era - the new helipad. But with no pool cameras present, much of the media did not carry any pictures and for those that did, there was no microphone to clearly pick up the president's remarks.

blocks.caption: Image caption, The TV network rotate coverage of White House events

blocks.text: The TV network rotate coverage of White House events
Why did US networks pull out of filming Trump?

Fox News Washington bureau chief Bryan Boughton, who currently holds the rotating role covering the White House, wrote in an email seen by the BBC that "effective today, the TV pool will not be covering events designated as pool coverage" of President Trump.
In a joint statement, the five networks said: "The public has a vital interest in receiving accurate, independent information about its government.
"No administration should restrict a news organisation because it objects to its reporting."
The First Amendment of the US Constitution protects speech and press freedoms.

It forbids the government from "abridging" the freedom of the press - language that courts have traditionally interpreted as preventing the government from discriminating against the media based on the content of their coverage.

CNN, Politico and MS NOW have filed a lawsuit against the Trump administration to "defend the principle that the government does not decide what the press reports". A hearing is scheduled for Wednesday.
In a joint statement on Monday, they said: "Without notice or process, the White House revoked our journalists' credentials because it objected to our reporting.
"Left unchallenged, this threatens press freedom and the public's right to independent journalism free from government interference."
Trump's speech to the United Nations on Tuesday will be unaffected by the boycott because it will be carried by outlets which are not part of the pool.
But the president's movements to and from his various New York events, which are usually filmed, could be subject to the blackout.
How has Trump reacted and what is Trump TV?
Responding to news of the lawsuit, Trump called the outlets "Third Rate Clowns" and "Crooked and Corrupt Press" that "trivialise and demean" his achievements.

"Fake News people and publications that only write negatively, and who violate our National Security by writing false and defamatory stories with unknown 'sources,' shouldn't be allowed access to the most important Office anywhere in the World," Trump wrote on his Truth Social platform.
He added that his team would file an appeal. Meanwhile the White House has launched Trump TV, a 24/7 stream on YouTube.
Its description reads: "Watch the Trump Administration's biggest moments all in one place."
So far, the channel has primarily consisted of replays of previous Trump speeches and rallies.
For now, the White House media slot has remained vacant and instead the conservative TV outlet, Real America's Voice, was listed as "secondary" crew on Trump's trip to New York.
Unlike the traditional pool, however, that outlet is under no obligation to share material with others and has operated unilaterally for its audience.
In February, the White House announced it was taking control of the press pool which has access to Trump and had for more than a century been managed by the White House Correspondents' Association.

The same month, the administration moved to bar Associated Press reporters and photographers from spaces where access is limited, such as the Oval Office or Air Force One, because of the outlet's usage of the term "Gulf of Mexico" instead of "Gulf of America". AP filed a lawsuit and the case remains ongoing.
There have been a few instances of other administrations attempting to limit certain outlets' access.
The Obama administration tried to exclude Fox News from participating in a press pool interview with an administration official in 2009.

But after pushback from the other four networks in the pool, Fox News was granted access. Unlike with Trump's exclusion of CNN, MS NOW and Politico, the Obama administration did not try to bar Fox News from all pool coverage, just one specific interview.

articles.title: Sara Duterte's GenCorp SALN disclosure 'admission against interest' -- House panel
articles.summary: Vice President Sara Duterte"s declaration of GenCorp. Industries Inc. as one of her business interests in her 2024 and 2025 Statements of Assets, Liabilities and Net Worth (SALNs), despite the…

blocks.text: Published September 22, 2026 7:31pm

Vice President Sara Duterte’s declaration of GenCorp. Industries Inc. as one of her business interests in her 2024 and 2025 Statements of Assets, Liabilities and Net Worth (SALNs) constitutes an admission against her interest and should be given greater evidentiary weight, the House prosecution panel said Tuesday.

House prosecution panel adviser and former Surigao del Norte Rep. Ace Barbers and panel spokesperson Zia Adiong said Duterte’s sworn declaration should carry more weight than the absence of her name in GenCorp.’s corporate records.

“In [regular] courts, when it's an admission against interest, it is supreme in terms of appreciation of the court because it is an admission that won't favor you and yet you admit to it. In the same application here, she declared in her SALN that she has business interest in GenCorp.,” Barbers said at a press conference.

Barbers made the statement after prosecution witness Rendell Sopeña, division chief of the Philippine Government Electronic Procurement System (PhilGEPS), told the Senate impeachment court that GenCorp. secured P35 million worth of government contracts while Duterte was Vice President.
“That would run contrary to her interest because she should have divested from businesses as provided by the Constitution,” he added.
Barbers was referring to Article VII, Section 13 of the 1987 Constitution, which states:

“The President, Vice-President, the Members of the Cabinet, and their deputies or assistants shall not, during said tenure, directly or indirectly, practice any other profession, participate in any business, or be financially interested in any contract with, or in any franchise, or special privilege granted by the Government or any subdivision, agency, or instrumentality thereof, including government-owned or controlled corporations or their subsidiaries.”
The same provision also states: “They shall strictly avoid conflict of interest in the conduct of their office.”
Adiong, for his part, said Duterte’s disclosure cannot be dismissed simply because her name does not appear in GenCorp.’s corporate filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC).
“The [one with] higher [weight] here is the one declaring the asset. That’s her SALN, she declared her interest there [in GenCorp.] for two years. That was not an honest mistake,” Adiong said.
“Besides, the SALN is executed under oath. That is why the law imposes sanctions if there is an untruthful [statement] or concealment of disclosure,” he added.

Also on Tuesday, the Vice President’s brother, Davao City Mayor Sebastian Duterte, said in a statement that the Davao City government’s transactions with GenCorp. amounted to more than P33.2 million across 19 contracts.

The mayor said the transactions were all above board and that he and other Davao City government officials “never had any knowledge of Vice President Sara Duterte holding an interest in ‘GenCorp. Industries Inc.’”— MCG, GMA News

articles.title: Iran war spreads through region as Trump seeks way out
articles.summary: Washington, Tehran and the Gulf states continue to pursue different objectives while searching for a way to end the Iran war.

image.caption: In addition to the Strait of Hormuz, the fighting is now affecting Saudi oil exports through the Red SeaImage: Majid Asgaripour/WANA/REUTERS

blocks.text: Nearly seven months into the Iran war, negotiations between Washington and Tehran have led nowhere, and the conflict has spread from the Strait of Hormuz to another strategically important shipping route.

In September, Iran-backed Houthi militia in Yemen took over critical positions on the Yemeni coast and are threatening Red Sea trade routes while launching attacks on targets in Saudi Arabia. This compounds a global energy crunch brought on by the Strait of Hormuz blockade.
Earlier in September, Saudi officials blamed Iran-backed militias in Iraq for blowing up the critical East-West oil pipeline.
According to The New York Times, Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman called US President Donald Trump on Sunday to once again urge him to intervene and stop the Houthi's rapid advance.

Trump is reported to have considered airstrikes against the Houthis at one point, but later abandoned the plans. This weekend, Fox News reported that Trump said the Houthi rebels had agreed not to attack US targets. The US news outlet Axios also reported that Trump had rejected a Saudi request for strikes against the Houthis the previous week.
Why can't Saudi Arabia stop the Houthis?

Against the backdrop of record high gasoline and diesel prices coming down hard on voters ahead of the November 3 US midterm elections, US President Donald Trump is under pressure to show results in the Iran war.

"President Trump wants to end the Iran war from a position that allows him to claim that Iran's nuclear and military capabilities have been significantly weakened, freedom of navigation has been restored, and Tehran has been forced back to the negotiating table," Iran expert Fatemeh Aman told DW.

Aman, who has worked with organizations including the Middle East Institute, the Atlantic Council, RFE/RL and Voice of America, however, added that a coherent strategy for achieving these objectives remains difficult to discern.

The US has imposed high military and economic costs on Iran and appears to have made progress in weakening the country's military capabilities. But Tehran has not capitulated and there is no lasting ceasefire agreement.

Trump is due to meet Chinese President Xi Jinping in Washington this week. China is by far the largest buyer of Iranian oil and an important political partner of Tehran. The US president is likely to bring up China's economic and financial ties with Iran and hope that Beijing will use its influence over Tehran — particularly when it comes to the security of shipping in the Strait of Hormuz.

At the same time, Trump has signaled that he is open to meeting Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, who is traveling to New York for the United Nations General Assembly. Senior representatives from the Gulf states are also expected in the US over the coming days.
According to Axios, Trump plans to discuss the Iran war with representatives of several Gulf states on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly.
Houthi gains in Yemen threaten key Red Sea shipping route
Gulf nations want regional stability

There is still no common position emerging between Iran and its Arab neighbors in the Gulf. A planned meeting involving Iran, the Gulf states and Iraq was canceled last week. The cancellation may be linked to the Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia.

"At first glance, there appears to be little common ground between Iran and the Gulf states," Farzan Sabet, a Middle East expert at the Geneva Graduate Institute, told DW. "But behind the scenes, there is at least a shared interest in preventing further military escalation."
The Gulf states recognize that they would be unlikely to prevail in a direct military confrontation with Iran, and generally favor de-escalation and a pragmatic easing of tensions with Tehran.
An agreement, however, is not currently in sight. In particular, Iran's demands for greater control over the Strait of Hormuz go too far from the perspective of the Gulf states.
The war in Yemen further limits the scope for rapprochement. Saudi Arabia, for example, is unlikely to make concessions while it remains under pressure from the Iran-aligned Houthis.
Is Iran set to become an economic outcast?
Iran's two-track strategy
A permanently hostile, US-backed coalition of Gulf states would be strategically costly for Tehran, Aman said.

She added Iran could pursue a two-track strategy: This would involve resisting a US-led regional containment architecture, while simultaneously offering the Gulf states an alternative model of regional security based on accommodation and dialogue.
"After all, the Gulf states are not only Iran's rivals but also its neighbors — and neither side can change that geographic reality," Aman said.
According to Iranian security official Mohsen Rezaei, Tehran is demanding that the US end the fighting on all fronts.

Tehran is also calling for the release of billions in frozen Iranian assets and the lifting of the naval blockade in the strait. Talks with Qatar and Oman are reportedly continuing. The Iranian regime is now waiting for a response from Trump. Whether these diplomatic signals can translate into a broader political process remains uncertain.
For now, the main obstacle is that Washington, Tehran and the Gulf states continue to pursue very different roadmaps for ending the months-long conflict.
This article was translated from German.

articles.title: Palace: Gov't not inclined to enact fare hike, but possibility is there
articles.summary: The Palace on Tuesday said the government is not inclined to pass fare hikes across different public utility vehicles (PUV), but has not closed the door on this proposal.

blocks.text: Published September 22, 2026 7:19pm
The Palace on Tuesday said the government is not inclined to pass fare hikes across different public utility vehicles (PUV), but has not closed the door on this proposal.
Several transport groups have called upon the government to allow the implementation of a fare hike following the oil price hike driven by the Middle East conflict.

“Mabigat po talaga kasi kung pagsasabay-sabayin lahat, so noon pa naman ang gusto ng Pangulo ay balanshado, tumaas man ang presyo ng krudo ay hindi naman masyadong mararamdaman ng ating mga commuters,” Palace Press Officer Claire Castro said.
(It is heavy to have everything happen all at once, so even then the President wants it balanced, even if the price of crude increases, it should not be felt by the commuters.)

Castro, citing Transportation Secretary Giovanni Lopez, said the government is exhausting every means to help both transport workers and commuters. Lopez, as quoted by Castro, said that raising the fare was a “last resort”.

“Hindi po kasi sa ngayon incline talaga na magtaas ng pamasahe para sa ating mga kababayan, pero hindi po naman sinasara ang pintuan patungkol po dito. Hangga’t kakayanin lang po na ibigay muna ang tulong sa ating mga tsuper sa transport sector nang hindi tataas ang pamasahe, iyon po muna ang ginagawa ng administrasyon,” Castro said.

(We are not inclined to raise the fare for our citizens, but we are not closing the door on this. As long as we can give help to our motorists in the transport sector without increasing the fare, this is what the administration will do.)
Excise tax suspension

The Department of Energy has certified that the conditions for the excise tax suspension have been met after crude oil has surpassed $80 dollars per barrel. They have also sent the required document to Malacañang.
Castro also said the decision on the suspension of the excise taxes will be out within the week.
“Nabigyan po tayo ng update patungkol po diyan at patapos na po ang kanilang rekomendasyon, siguro most probably by this week ay mabibigay na po nila sa Pangulo,” Castro said.
(We were given an update there and after their recommendation, probably by the end of this week the president will give them.)
Castro assured that President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr. will immediately implement the suspension if needed. — BAP, GMA News

articles.title: Turkey: Several pupils injured in shooting outside school
articles.summary: The shooter, a pupil, allegedly took a rifle and shot indiscriminately at his schoolmates in front of their high school. Turkey was shocked by two back-to-back school shootings earlier this year.

image.caption: Footage posted online showed a male carrying a rifle near the schoolImage: DHA

blocks.text: A shooting near a high school in Turkey's Manisa province resulted in at least 11 injured pupils, two of whom were in critical condition on Tuesday, Justice Minister Akin Gurlek said.
The shooter, a pupil at the school, was arrested together with both of his parents and his grandfather.
What do we know about the shooting incident?
The suspect is said to have taken the weapon from his grandparents' house, with his grandfather believed to have had a licence for it.
Local authorities said the attack took place at the Inci Uzmez Vocational and Technical Anatolian High School in the Turgutlu district at about 08:00am local time (07:00 CET).
The motive for the shooting is also under investigation. Some reports suggest the student had suffered from bullying.

blocks.caption: Two back-to-back school shootings in April left around 10 killed and dozens more injuredImage: Ensar Ozdemir/REUTERS

blocks.text: "When the ​security of our children is the issue, it is not possible for any ​negligence, any irresponsibility to be overlooked," the minister posted on his X account.

"The ‌circumstances under which the child obtained the gun used in the attack, the conditions of the weapon's storage, the parents' obligations regarding care ‌and supervision, and allegations of bullying prior to the incident ‌are ​being investigated thoroughly and from multiple angles," Gurlek added.
Footage posted online showed a male carrying a rifle near the school, while police told families to stay away from the area.
Gun control tightened after school shootings
School shootings are rare in Turkey, but this year alone saw two back-to-back shootings that shocked the nation.
Two school shootings that took place in April resulted in the tightening of gun controls and the increase of security measures at educational facilities as the academic year started last week.
Several students and their teacher were killed in one of the attacks, with the other resulting in 16 people being injured.
According to Interior Minister Mustafa Ciftci, 31,000 school supervisors and police officers on duty were assigned to school seen as being at risk, as per a new measure introduced only on Monday.
President Recep Tayyip Erdogan responded to the latest shooting attack by promising even tighter gun controls.
"When we look at similar attacks around the world, especially in the United States, we see one of the perpetrators' aims is to terrorise society," the Turkish leader said.

articles.title: Jollibee enters the menu as impeach court scrutinizes Sara Duterte businesses
articles.summary: 'Bida ang sarap, bida ang ebidensya,' prosecutor Terry Ridon quips

blocks.text: Graphics by Nico Villarete/Rappler
'Bida ang sarap, bida ang ebidensya,' prosecutor Terry Ridon quips
Even the country’s top fast food chain was not spared in the expansive investigation into Vice President Sara Duterte’s alleged unexplained wealth.
Could Jollibee hold a piece of the smoking gun that the prosecution has been searching for to remove her from office?

Jollibee was implicated in the mess because documents show that its Bolton Street branch in Davao City is owned by Gencorp Industries Inc., described in one of government documents as a franchisee of the casual dining giant.

Duterte said in her sworn Statement of Assets, Liabilities, and Net Worth (SALN) that she is a stockholder of Gencorp, although her name is not in Securities and Exchange Commission documents (SEC) filings of the company.

Other companies associated with the Vice President or her husband Mans Carpio are Metro City Chow Food Corporation, City Hall King Chow Foods Corporation, Timesquare Bee Foods Corp., and Great Jolly Times Food Corp.
The names of several of these companies appear to echo those of Jollibee and its sister fast-food chain, Chowking.

“This P2.1 billion in sales — these are restaurants, right? Are they Jollibee or Chowking?” Senator Kiko Pangilinan asked. “I would assume there are many Jollibee and Chowking franchises, which is why sales reached billions over a period of time.”
“One of the financial statements that the witness identified yesterday contains the word ‘Jollibee’ in reference to Gencorp,” prosecutor Erwin Matib said. “Yes, there are franchises.”
Jollibee Davao Bolton is a known hangout spot of the Dutertes. It is in the same building as the listed address of Gencorp.

Rappler previously reported that Gencorp has cornered at least P14 million in contracts with Davao City Hall since 2022, coinciding with the time that Sara became VP, and her brother Sebastian assumed the mayorship of their hometown.

The Davao City mayor later not only confirmed the existence of the deals, but even updated the actual total value of the contracts bagged by Gencorp — P33 million over 19 contracts. Philippine Government Electronic Procurement System division chief Rendell Sopeña told the impeachment court that there are 15 Gencorp-Davao City deals worth P34 million in its database.

The arrangement raises questions on conflict of interest, and potential violation of the Constitution. The 1987 charter explicitly prohibits the Vice President from having business interests while in office.
The Jollibee connection did not escape the prosecution and her critics, which used its slogan to take a swipe at the Vice President.
“Bida ang sarap, bida ang ebidensiya (the star is the flavor, the star is the evidence),” prosecutor Terry Ridon said.

blocks.caption: Jollibee enters the menu as impeach court scrutinizes Sara Duterte businesses

blocks.text: “Inday, pa-Jollibee ka naman diyan (Inday, how about treating us to Jollibee),” former presidential adviser Ronald Llamas said in jest on Facebook.
Spectators of the trial might just be craving two things after Tuesday’s proceedings: a one-piece Chickenjoy, and an explanation from the Vice President. – Rappler.com

blocks.text: US TV networks suspend White House pool coverage over Trump media ban
Ariana Baio
The major US television news outlets agreed to suspend their video coverage of Donald Trump after the administration banned journalists from several outlets from entering the White House grounds.
The collective decision came after the barred outlets – CNN, MS Now and Politico – sued the administration on Monday, saying the president’s actions were a violation of their first amendment rights.

The ban was an extraordinary escalation of Trump’s battle against news outlets. After a coalition of networks including ABC, CBS, Fox News and NBC – which along with CNN form a press “pool” that share the responsibilities of capturing and distributing footage of the president carried by news outlets worldwide – announced they would cease coverage in solidarity with the barred outlets, the White House promoted its own feed online, branding it “Trump TV”. The channel purported to show “top past moments, announcements, and the latest and greatest from the administration all in one place”.
“Get real-time updates and live events streamed DIRECTLY to your phone,” the White House posted on social media. “No noise. Just the news that matters most – straight from the Trump Administration.”

It is extremely rare for a president to travel or make public appearances without the accompaniment of a representative from the White House television pool. Network cameras have provided coverage of the president since 1950.

On Monday, the ban against CNN meant that no broadcaster was covering Trump’s midday ribbon-cutting to unveil a new White House helipad. Although the White House provided a livestream, without professional boom mics and audio setup, the president’s remarks were inaudible over the sounds of a helicopter’s engine running in the background.

The president abruptly announced his ban against outlets this weekend in a Truth Social post, saying he had enough of “purposely negative stories” about him. Journalists had their press badges confiscated by Secret Service on Saturday.
Trump set for UN meetings with war on agenda as speech looms
Hello and welcome to the US politics live blog.
Donald Trump is expected to ⁠start the day with a speech to assembled delegates at the UN General Assembly, before meeting with no fewer than 11 world leaders, bilaterally or in group settings.

While the contents of his speech are unknown, Trump last year caused a ⁠stir with a combative address, telling the audience that their countries were “going to hell” for, among other things, climate policy and mass migration.
The president is then set for a whirlwind schedule of meetings with ⁠leaders from four continents on Tuesday.
It comes against the backdrop of an unstable Middle East and a four-and-a-half-year-old war in Ukraine that shows no signs of abating.

Trump will meet with British prime minister Andy Burnham, Ukrainian ‌president Volodymyr Zelenskyy, Venezuela’s interim leader Delcy ‌Rodriguez, Danish prime minister Mette Frederiksen, Greenland prime minister Jens-Frederik Nielsen and the representatives of the Gulf states of the United Arab Emirates, ‌Saudi Arabia, Oman, Bahrain, Kuwait and Qatar.

In the evening, he may meet dozens more leaders, albeit briefly, during a leaders’ reception. Trump met with French president Emmanuel Macron on Monday and additions to his Tuesday schedule are possible.
Here, my colleague Robert Tait provides some analysis on what may be expected from Trump’s address:
In other developments:

items: The major US television news outlets agreed to suspend their video coverage of Donald Trump after the administration banned journalists from several outlets from entering the White House grounds. Newsrooms including the New York Times and the Washington Post also decided to hold off on publishing or distributing still photographs taken as part of the White House pool coverage on Monday until midnight as part of the collective effort. More here.

The barred outlets – CNN, MS Now and Politico – sued the administration on Monday, saying the president’s actions were a violation of their first amendment rights. The parties are seeking a temporary restraining order that would immediately lift the ban – and return access for the journalists – while the case plays out. More here.

Trump is bracing for a loss in the lawsuit brought by the three media organizations, as he considers that the judge presiding over the case – his own appointee – previously ordered the White House to restore credentials for journalist Jim Acosta. “In other words, almost without question and, as usual, we’ll go for appeal,” he wrote on Truth Social.

Trump said that he hoped Zohran Mamdani would be a “great mayor” for New York, an unusually warm assessment of the democratic socialist leader whom the president and his Republican allies have spent months holding up as a symbol of the Democratic party’s alleged embrace of “communism” ahead of the November midterms. More here.

The Venezuelan man who was shot by a federal immigration officer in Texas on Sunday spoke out from detention on Monday afternoon when he was able to call his lawyer, in the middle of a press conference, and plead for better medical care. Wilber Rafael Garcés Pérez, 28, was taken from a hospital in Austin into Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) detention, even though he apparently still has a bullet lodged near his spine and is in much discomfort. items: Jean Claude Saclag won a silver medal in the men's traditional -65kg class at the 2026 Asian Games, marking the Philippines' best finish so far.
Saclag initially knocked down his opponent, Otabek Rajabov, but ultimately lost by unanimous decision after Rajabov utilized his ground game effectively.
The Philippines has now secured one silver and three bronze medals in the games, with notable performances from other athletes including a women's kata team in karate.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.
MANILA, Philippines – Mixed martial arts standout Jean Claude Saclag missed out on a coveted gold medal but delivered the Philippines’ best finish so far in the 2026 Asian Games in Nagoya, Japan.

Saclag settled for silver, falling prey to Tajikistan’s Otabek Rajabov via unanimous decision in the final of the men’s traditional -65kg class at the Nagoya City Inae Sports Center on Tuesday, September 22.

A pride of Kalinga and Benguet, Saclag scored an early knockdown as he dropped Rajabov with a left hook to the head before the Tajik regained his bearings and banked on his prolific ground game en route to the victory.
Rajabov, an unbeaten professional MMA fighter with a 6-0 record, pulled off multiple takedowns the rest of the way to neutralize Saclag.

“It was really unfortunate. We really prepared for the ground game. I gave it my all. At least we got the silver and we’re not going home without a medal,” Saclag said in a mix of Filipino and English during the post-match Cignal broadcast.
An accomplished fighter in multiple combat disciplines, Saclag matched his silver in the 2014 edition in Incheon, South Korea, where he represented the country in wushu.
The medal is an early birthday gift for Saclag, who is also a three-time kickboxing champion in the Southeast Asian Games. He turns 32 on Friday, September 25.
Saclag reached the championship match after beating Saudi Arabia’s Saud Fawaz Almolhem in the quarterfinals and Japan’s Daisuke Murayama in the semifinals.

Earlier in the day, the karate trio of Rebecca Cyril Torres, Ysabielle Arrogante, and Samantha Emmanuelle Veguillas bagged another bronze for the country, earning a podium finish in the women’s kata team event.
The Filipinas absorbed a 5-0 loss to Iran in the semifinals but redeemed themselves with a 4-1 victory over Thailand in the bronze-medal match at the Toyohashi Gymnasium.
“It has been a long journey. My teammates have gone through a lot of hardships,” said Torres in Filipino.
“We have suffered a lot of losses over the years, but we just perform and fight until the end.”

The Philippines now has one silver and three bronzes, the other two medals coming from the women’s soft tennis team of Bien Zoleta, Princess Catindig, Hilary Paas, Shyryn Salazar, and Christy Sañosa, and mixed martial artist Carlos Alvarez. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Impeachment court might defer vote on conviction threshold if senators need more time
articles.summary: The Senate impeachment court can defer the scheduled September 23 voting on the threshold needed for a conviction, court spokesperson Regie Tongol said.

blocks.text: Published September 22, 2026 6:14pm
The Senate impeachment court can defer the scheduled September 23 voting on the threshold needed for a conviction, court spokesperson Regie Tongol said.

Tongol said that this is because there are Senator judges who have appealed to their colleagues for more time to decide, given that the oral arguments on the matter will only be conducted also on September 23.

“There are Senator judges who are appealing for additional time [before making the decision] because the parties [to the case] might raise additional arguments which were not put forward by the amici curiae. They said they might need to study it further over the weekend to be fully evaluate the merits ahead of deciding on their vote,” Tongol said in a press conference.

Amici curiae are the "friends of the court" invited to speak before the Senate impeachment court on the matter of the conviction threshold in the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte: former Supreme Court Chief Justices Hilario Davide, Jr. Artemio Panganiban and Reynato Puno, and retired Supreme Court Associate Justice Adolf Azcuna.
“Hindi po malayo sa posibilidad na…maaari ring may humingi ng deferment po ng vote tomorrow at ma-reschedule iyong votation na kaysa tomorrow, some other time next week,” Tongol added.
(It's not outside the realm of possibility that a deferment of the vote may be requested tomorrow, and the votation deferred to some other time next week instead of tomorrow.)
The legal luminaries were invited to weigh in on whether the Constitution requires a definite 16 votes from Senator judges for a conviction.
Article 11, Section 6 of the 1987 Constitution states that “no person shall be convicted without the concurrence of two-thirds of all the Members of the Senate.”

Davide, Panganiban and Puno all said that 16 is not the threshold, given that the Constitution states a fraction—two-thirds—and not a number, in determining the threshold for conviction. Likewise, the three said that allowing those absent to vote would be unfair, if not an injustice, to the Filipino people since an impartial judge needs to evaluate the evidence for them to be able to make a sound judgment.

Only Azcuna advanced the position of retaining the 16-vote threshold as earlier ruled by Senate impeachment court presiding officer Francis Escudero, saying that moving the threshold should only happen if a member of members of the Senate dies.

Escudero’s ruling of 16 votes as threshold has since been challenged by Senator Erwin Tulfo, given that four of the 24 Senators have not been present to participate in the ongoing impeachment trial of the Vice President.
Senators Jinggoy Estrada and Rodante Marcoleta are detained on plunder and other related charges due to their alleged involvement in flood control and undeclared campaign donations, respectively.

Senator Ronald dela Rosa, on the other hand, is nowhere to be found amid a standing warrant of arrest issued against him by the International Criminal Court due to his alleged involvement in the drug war deaths.
Senator Loren Legarda, for her part, is on an extended medical leave abroad due to a lung ailment.

While Azcuna was the lone dissenter in changing the threshold, all the amici curiae agreed that the Senate impeachment court has the authority to determined the voting threshold needed for conviction because the Constitution provides that the Senate has the sole power to try and decide impeachment cases. — BM, GMA News

articles.title: House approves P975.96-billion DepEd budget for 2027
articles.summary: The House of Representatives approved on Tuesday the proposed P975.96-billion budget of the Department of Education (DepEd) for fiscal year 2027.

blocks.text: Published September 22, 2026 6:07pm
The House of Representatives approved on Tuesday the proposed P975.96-billion budget of the Department of Education (DepEd) for fiscal year 2027.
This allocation for the Education Department represents 13.55% of the proposed national budget for 2027, according to Appropriations Committee Vice Chair Rep. Maria Carmen Zamora.
“Once again, this single largest allocation of any department in the government as part of the education sector, consistent with the mandate of the Constitution,” Zamora said.
“It affirms that this house and this admin continue to treat education not as an expense but as the nation's most important investment,” she added.
Under DepEd’s budget, the highlighted major items include the School-Based Feeding Program (SBFP), government assistance and subsidies, and teacher promotion.
The SBFP was allocated P11.4 billion, eyed to provide public school learners with nutritious meals, addressing malnutrition while improving classroom attendance.

ACT Teachers Party-list Representative Antonio Tinio highlighted a 55% slash to the feeding program’s funding, while Gabriela Party-list Representative Sarah Elago pointed out a P14-billion overall drop in its allocation.

When asked how the budget cut would impact operations, Zamora explained that the feeding program’s duration will be trimmed from 180 days to 120 days and restricted primarily to kindergarten students.

“This will affect the number of days in the implementation, so instead na nasa 180 days magiging 120 days na lang 'yung implementation and will be limited only for kindergarten learners in terms of universal coverage,” Zamora said.

(This will affect the number of days in the implementation, so instead of 180 days, the implementation will be reduced to 120 days and will be limited only to kindergarten learners in terms of universal coverage.)
In 2026, the SBFP received a P25.7-billion budget. Elago urged fellow lawmakers to restore the program’s funding to its 2026 level to prevent a reduction in services.

“Sinusuportahan ng representasyon na ito ang pagre-restore ng pondo para dito sa School-Based Feeding Program doon sa level niya sa 2026 para mamentena po natin kung ano na currently yung ating binibigay na napakahalagang serbisyo sa mga learners,” Elago said.
(This representation supports the restoration of funds for the School-Based Feeding Program to its 2026 level so we can maintain the essential services we currently provide to our learners.)
Among other key allocations, DepEd’s government assistance and subsidies received P38.12 billion.
Meanwhile, P12.09 billion was set aside to support the expanded career progression program, paving the way for the promotion and professional advancement of qualified public school teachers.
DepEd remains the largest beneficiary in the proposed 2027 budget, according to the Department of Budget and Management.
In 2026, the agency received a P1.015-trillion budget, marking the highest allocation in its history.

This budget approval by the lower chamber does not finalize DepEd’s 2027 funding. The budget will still undergo scrutiny during the bicameral conference committee between the House and Senate, where the final version of the General Appropriations Act will be reconciled and finalized. — BAP, GMA News

blocks.text: Russia and Ukraine traded strikes targeting infrastructure overnight, ahead of a United Nations General Assembly where the war in Ukraine is due to be widely discussed.
Russian strikes on Ukraine overnight into Tuesday killed four people, Ukrainian officials said, while also cutting the electricity supply to thousands.

The strikes took place in the cities Dnipro, Kryvyi Rih and Pavlohrad in the southeastern region of Dnipropetrovsk, regional governor Oleksandr Hanzha said on Telegram. The barrage included anti-ship and ballistic missiles, four cruise missiles and 212 drones.
DW witnesses Ukrainian train evacuation
The region of Dnipropetrovsk is the country's industrial heartland, where major production industries are located, including steel-making and machine building.
In the city of Dnipro, four people were killed and six were injured. According to Hanzha, the strike also damaged a local business and a warehouse.
Ukraine strikes Russian oil refinery; 1 killed
In Russia, Ukrainian drones killed one person and injured four in the Samara region, local authorities said. The region is home to important facilities, including oil refineries.
Moscow's Defense Ministry said it had intercepted 297 drones over various regions in Russia overnight.
Samara is located some 1,000 kilometers southeast of Russian capital Moscow.
Zelenskyy attends UN General Assembly
Russia and Ukraine have both stepped up attacks recently, as the war has dragged on for four and a half years with no end in sight.
Both parties deny targeting civilians, while also blaming each other for civilian casualties.

The latest attacks come as Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy is planning to meet US counterpart Donald Trump in New York on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly. Russian President Vladimir Putin is not expected at the UN General Assembly.

articles.title: Male infertility is 'grossly underreported'
articles.summary: It's not all on women anymore — doctors do test men for sperm count and motility. But still too few men get checked, possibly due to a misconception that a healthy sex life means healthy sperm.…

image.caption: It just takes one out 16 million sperm, but many men can't even manage that Image: ktsdesign/Panthermedia/IMAGO

blocks.text: Sperm counts have fallen globally by more than 51% since 1973, and the decline is accelerating. That's according to a 2026 review of studies published in the journal Antioxidants. But men are less likely to get tested than women for infertility.
"Male infertility is understated. It is so huge a problem," said Edidiong Akang, a reproductive biologist at the University of Lagos, Nigeria.

In a study led by Akang and published in the journal Scientific Reports in 2023, he and his colleagues analyzed semen samples from more than 17,000 men and found that the quality of sperm shape and size (known as sperm morphology) had deteriorated by about 50% between 2010 and 2019.
Sperm motility (how well it swims to the female egg) had also dropped significantly — in Nigeria, for example, by 87% in that same period.
And yet, as Akang told DW, the male share of infertility is "grossly underreported" and, as a result, misunderstood.
What affects a man's fertility?

Male fertility depends on a healthy sperm shape, size, motility, and its concentration and count. The latter is often used as an indication of male fertility because many millions try to reach the egg but only one or few make it. They need to be strong swimmers.
Why do some healthy embryos fail to implant in the uterus?
These factors depend on other, underlying health conditions: Male infertility can be caused by weight gain, stress, poor sleep, smoking, microplastics and cannabis use.
Weight gain in particular effects the testes (also: testicles), which produce sperm and hormones like testosterone.
The testes function best at two degrees centigrade cooler than the rest of the body. Fat raises the temperature, and that can affect the sperm — its concentration, count and motility.
Why male infertility often goes undiagnosed

Male sexual health is often overlooked, possibly because men under the age of 40 don't generally have a regular reason to get checked — if you're older than 40, you may get your prostate checked annually. But even a urologist won't check your sperm count unless you ask them.
Women, on the other hand, get a monthly signal — their menstrual cycle — and may be able to infer from that that something is wrong.
A man gets no such natural signals about his fertility until he tries to conceive with a woman. And by then he may be 30 or 40, when some health outcomes are hard to reverse.
Riffat Bibi, a clinical embryologist who has led an IVF laboratory in Pakistan for 17 years, described what men often say on arrival: "Okay, check my wife first."
Sometimes a mother-in-law brings the daughter-in-law, which also suggests that the mother-in-law thinks: It can't be my son's fault.
And some patients "feel sexual activity is equivalent to fertility, which it is not," said Bibi.
Roughly 80% of Bibi's cases now involve a male factor, far above the 50-50 split long assumed, and her laboratory has had to adapt, she said.

They are also seeing this development in IVF (in vitro fertilization) treatment. Sperm has become so poor that nearly all her clients need an embryologist to pick a single sperm and inject it directly into the egg.
But there is another factor than many men don't talk about much: synthetic testosterone — or steroids.
IVF explained: Process, costs & risks
Testosterone shuts down sperm production
Some men, keen on a muscley body, suppress their own sperm production unknowingly by taking anabolic steroids, a synthetic form of testosterone.

The appeal of anabolic steroids is straightforward, said Harrison Pope, a Harvard Medical School researcher: Steroids enhance athletic performance. A steroid user, who drinks, smokes and skips half of his workouts can outperform a dedicated, clean athlete.
Pope, who has studied steroids for three decades, said "they are highly effective."
But what you gain in athletic performance, you lose in fertility, because an over-supply of testosterone can shut down sperm production.
A healthy body will keep testosterone levels in balance. Too little testosterone can also impede sperm production.
Sperm production can restart if you stop taking testosterone supplements, but Pope said it depends on your age, and much you were taking and for how long.
Occasional steroid users usually regain a "normal" sperm count. The World Health Organization considers a normal sperm count to be about 16 million sperm per milliliter of semen (or higher).
Heavy, long-term steroid users, meanwhile, often do not recover or return to normal sperm production.

Users typically take steroids in cycles – weeks on the drug, followed by a a break to let the body recover. But when Dutch researchers followed 100 men through one cycle of steroids and for a year after, they found two-thirds still had very low sperm counts, some had no sperm at all, and a year later, their counts had still not returned to normal.

Not everyone takes steroids, and yet falling sperm counts still occur. Take India, for example, where Chirag Bhandari, runs the Institute of Andrology and Sexual Health in Jaipur. Bhandari estimates that steroids account for less than 0.1% of the country's falling sperm counts. Overweight, heat-stress and smoking are usually the cause.

If a man is tested early, his sperm count will often return to normal within six to twelve months, both Bhandari and Bibi said. But the longer the problem goes undetected, the less likely that becomes.

articles.title: PH, EU on ‘clear path’ to free trade agreement. How close is a deal, really?
articles.summary: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen declares that the EU and the Philippines have 'just agreed' on a free trade deal that could eventually make nearly all bilateral goods trade…

blocks.text: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen declares that the EU and the Philippines have 'just agreed' on a free trade deal that could eventually make nearly all bilateral goods trade tariff-free, with signing targeted for 2027
MANILA, Philippines – A “substantial agreement,” a “clear path” toward conclusion, and from the European Commission president herself: “We just agreed on a EU-Philippines free trade deal!”

After years of negotiations, officials from the Philippines and European Union (EU) spoke on Tuesday, September 22, with resounding confidence that a long-awaited free trade agreement (FTA) between the two was within reach.
But beneath the diplomatic jargon, is there actually an FTA already? Not quite.

Philippine Trade Secretary Cristina Roque and European Commissioner for Trade and Economic Security Maroš Šefčovič announced that both sides had reached a “substantial agreement” following a video call, with their joint statement describing the development as a “breakthrough” that puts the FTA on a “clear path towards its formal conclusion in the coming months.”
Negotiating teams were instructed to finalize the agreement “as soon as possible.”

Meanwhile, European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen struck a more emphatic tone in a post on X after speaking with President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., declaring that the two sides had “just agreed” on a free trade deal. The Commission’s official readout of their September 21 call was more cautious, saying the Philippines and EU were “about to conclude talks” on an FTA.

So what’s left to do? A separate European Commission press release states that the Philippines and EU still have to “now finalize the negotiations on the basis of the substantial agreement reached today, including determining its implementation and finalizing technical details.”
There is already a target for the next big milestone. European Commission President von der Leyen said she looks forward to returning to the Philippines in 2027 to sign the FTA.

The European Commission said the deal would remove or cut tariffs on more than 94% of product categories, covering over 97% of the goods the Philippines and EU currently trade by value. It also covers services and investment, digital trade, intellectual property, food and product standards, sustainability, energy, and raw materials.

It would also establish rules allowing foreign bidders access to the Philippine government procurement market, which the EU described as opening that market to foreign bidders “for the first time ever.”
For Filipinos, the most immediate question is whether an FTA could make European products cheaper.

Potentially, yes. The EU says some of its major industrial exports to the Philippines include machinery and appliances, transport equipment, medicines and medical appliances, while agricultural exports include pork, poultry, dairy products and spirits.

Cutting Philippine tariffs on these goods could reduce their landed cost and increase competition or consumer choice. But an FTA doesn’t automatically mean cheaper shelf prices. It is still unclear which individual products will get immediate tariff elimination and which may be phased in over several years.
The EU was the Philippines’ fourth-largest trading partner in 2025, accounting for 8.3% of total Philippine goods trade.

Bilateral merchandise trade reached €17.6 billion (P1.27 trillion)* in 2025, consisting of €9.5 billion (P684.3 billion) in EU imports from the Philippines and €8.1 billion (P583.4 billion) in EU exports to the country. Services trade reached another €10.3 billion (P741.9 billion) in 2024, while the stock of EU foreign direct investment in the Philippines stood at €15.4 billion (P1.11 trillion).

The negotiations themselves have been more than a decade in the making. Talks were launched in 2015, stalled after a second negotiating round in 2017, and revived in March 2024 after both sides conducted a technical stocktaking exercise. – Rappler.com
*€1 = P72.0305 based on the September 22, 2026 rate of the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas’ Daily Reference Exchange Rate Bulletin

articles.title: FACT CHECK: Bill postponing 2026 barangay, SK polls not yet a law as of September 22
articles.summary: In a September 18 statement, the Commission on Elections said the November 2026 barangay and Sangguniang Kabataan elections will proceed as there is yet no law for its postponement

blocks.text: Claim: The bill postponing the November 2 barangay and Sangguniang Kabataan elections (BSKE) became a law on September 21, prompting the Commission on Elections (Comelec) to announce the suspension of the filing of certificates of candidacy.
Why we fact-checked this: A Facebook account named “Rolando Hagos,” which currently has over 20,000 followers, has made multiple posts bearing the false claim.
His most recent post says: “Comelec, kinansel na ang filing of candidacy ng mga tatakbo para sa barangay election.”
(The Comelec has cancelled the filing of certificates of candidacy for those running in the barangay elections.)
He also made other posts earlier claiming, “September 21 ganap ng batas ang postponement ng BSKE. November 2028 na.”
(The postponement of the BSKE became law on September 21. It is now set for November 2028.)
Both posts have received a total of 2,000 reactions, more than 600 comments, and less than 100 shares, as of writing.
The facts: In a September 18 statement posted on Facebook, Comelec Chairman George Erwin said the BSKE will push through on November 2, unless a new law postponing the election will be enacted.

In his statement, the chair explained: “Tuloy na tuloy ang (BSKE) eleksyon hanggang sa araw na ‘to, sapagkat ‘yun po ang batas. ‘Yan po ang ikalat n’yo. ‘Yan po ay hindi fake news; totoo po ‘yan. Wala pa tayong batas. Batas ang ating hahanapin.”

(The election will definitely push through as scheduled, because that is what the law says. Please spread the word. That is not fake news; it is the truth. We do not have a new law yet; the law is what we look for.)

The chair also noted that unless such a law is passed, the filing of certificates of candidacy scheduled from September 28 to October 5 will push through. The commission also said that it will continue its preparation for the BSKE, in line with the provisions of Republic Act No. 12232 setting the date of elections on November 2.

The misleading posts about the postponement of the BSKE circulated after the Senate approved on September 14 a bill fixing the term of barangay and SK officials to five years, effectively moving the polls to the second Monday of November starting in 2028.

The proposed measure is now in the hands of President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., who may sign the bill into law or veto it. It may also lapse into law if he does not act on the measure within 30 days of receiving it.

No official government announcement or credible media report shows that the bill has already been signed into law. Palace Press Officer Claire Castro also said Marcos will review the provisions of the bill before making a decision.

BSKE postponement: This is not the first time proposals have been made to postpone the BSKE. In 2022, the elections originally scheduled for December were moved to October 2023, under Republic Act No. 11935. Following this, Republic Act No. 12232 was signed into law in August 2025 pushing the December 2025 BSKE to November 2026.
The current proposal, which aims to move the scheduled November 2026 elections to 2028, has drawn opposition from election watchdog groups.
Debunked: Rappler has previously debunked other false claims related to earlier and upcoming elections:

items: FACT CHECK: Comelec debunks claim of ACMs altering votes in Lanao del Sur
FACT CHECK: Photos of Sara Duterte visiting MILF camp ahead of 2026 polls are fake
FACT CHECK: News of 39 soldiers held by MILF is from 2023, not recent

blocks.text: – Jerome Santos/Rappler.com
John Jerome Santos is a research and data volunteer writer at Rappler. He is a fourth year Bachelor of Science in Accountancy student at the Dr. Gloria Lacson Foundation Colleges of Cabanatuan City.

Keep us aware of suspicious Facebook pages, groups, accounts, websites, articles, or photos in your network by contacting us at factcheck@rappler.com. Let us battle disinformation one Fact Check at a time.

It’s Tuesday, 22 September 2026, it’s Jakub Krupa here, and this is Europe Live.

items: 14m agoEU deadlocked over plans to remove two Russian billionaires from sanctions list
17m agoMorning opening: Welcome to New York

blocks.text: EU deadlocked over plans to remove two Russian billionaires from sanctions list

blocks.caption: Jennifer Rankin

blocks.text: Jennifer Rankin
in Brussels

The EU is deadlocked over a plan to remove two Russian billionaires, Alisher Usmanov and Mikhail Fridman, from its sanctions list as part of a bitterly disputed deal to keep broader restrictions in place on nearly 3,000 people and companies accused of enabling Vladimir Putin’s war on Ukraine.

blocks.caption: Russian president Vladimir Putin shakes hands with Russian businessman and founder of USM Holdings Alisher Usmanov during an awarding ceremony at the Kremlin in Moscow, Russia in 2018. Photograph: SPUTNIK/Reuters

blocks.text: Ambassadors from the EU’s 27 member states failed to reach agreement at a meeting early on Tuesday – their third session in around 24 hours on the topic. The senior diplomats will reconvene later today just hours ahead of a legal deadline.
Without an agreement sanctions on nearly 3,000 people and entities accused of supporting the war on Ukraine will lapse at the end of Tuesday 22 September.
The list includes Vladimir Putin, foreign minister Sergei Lavrov, Duma deputies, Russia’s major banks, energy companies and military industrial complex.
The EU can also agree a short-term extension pending a longer agreement and has already prolonged the deadline by one week. One diplomat suggested that was a likely outcome.
Latvia emerged as the last-minute block on an agreement. Like many member states the Baltic state has strong objections to the de-listings, which are demanded by France and Slovakia.

Latvia’s prime minister Andris Kulbergs tweeted late Monday night that he could not accept the proposed compromise – the de-listings of Usmanov and Fridman in exchange for a 36-month extension of the blacklist of nearly 3,000 names, far longer than the usual six-month rollover.
He said:
“Extending sanctions for 36 months would be the right step. However, the price for it must not be simply striking both individuals from the sanctions list. Latvia cannot accept SUCH an offer.”

blocks.caption: Latvian prime minister Andris Kulbergs attends the European Arctic Summit in Rovaniemi, Finland last week. Photograph: Kaisa Siren/EPA

blocks.text: He added that his foreign minister, Baiba Braže, would work with “Brussels and Paris to find a solution SUITABLE for Latvia’s interests. We will seek support in the EUROPEAN UNION for Latvia’s position”.

When details of the expected deal emerged on Monday, Ukraine’s foreign minister, Andrii Sybiha, said the delisting was “unacceptable and would send the wrong signal to Moscow at a time when pressure needs to increase”.

France infuriated and stunned EU member states by joining Slovakia’s populist government in petitioning for Usmanov’s de-listing earlier this month. France has told EU diplomats only that the delisting is on national security grounds. The Financial Times has reported that it is linked to a prisoner exchange deal with Azerbaijan involving the release of French nationals.

Azerbaijan, along with the Organisation of Turkic States, has previously lobbied western decision-makers to remove Usmanov from sanctions listings, describing him as “a renowned philanthropist” who has built bridges between the West, Central Asia and wider Turkic world. Slovakia began lobbying for Usmanov and fellow billionaire Mikhail Fridman to be removed from the EU sanctions list in the summer.
Luxembourg has argued that Fridman should come off the list, if Usmanov is removed. Fridman is seeking $16bn in damages from Luxembourg for freezing his assets.
